# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Victims of CSE scandal deserve "full, unvarnished truth" from Grooming Gangs Inquiry](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Islam · The Star*

Victims and campaigners are calling for the Grooming Gangs Inquiry to publish the full truth about child sexual exploitation scandals, including what police, councils and social services failed to do.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** 'Sarah' was subjected to exactly this kind of abuse: groomed from the age of 15, repeatedly raped, forced into sharia marriages, forcibly converted to Islam and then failed by the authorities.

**Who this hits:** This affects victims who have waited years to be believed, and families who still do not know whether the same failures could happen in their town. It also affects Christians who want truth told without victims being silenced by fear of being called racist or Islamophobic.

**Angle:** We should say plainly that victims deserve the whole truth, including religious and cultural factors where they are relevant. Viewers will understand why euphemisms and official defensiveness protect institutions, not children, and why they should demand that MPs back a genuinely fearless inquiry.

**Opening line:** "What if the truth about grooming gangs is still being softened?"

**Title:** *Grooming gangs inquiry: victims deserve the whole truth*

### 2. [Christians calls on British Medical Association to drop opposition to NHS trans guidance](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwgFBVV95cUxQSGxVblNSQXM0V2tyOTdBS3RveW1PdDRPeTBNbTRwQnBhXzNlYm4za0JjYW9aM0RWX3FnOXRqSWYzc2NldGdHMllvN1RGWl9qMk16aHo5eHFKME9xWElCc1JTSjJfdlBGdUdFRU9Uc1ljZjE0X2JmX0ttR3dxZkRWYmx4c1JfY3JPdnduTjdubVV3dDljNEJhbUhEM19KYmlpcTU4bE5nT2MzMVNXV3FIWmVZR1BzX0swaU5LX2h1MmYtQQ?oc=5)
*Gender · www.christiantoday.com*

Christian voices are urging the British Medical Association to stop opposing NHS guidance on transgender issues, including guidance intended to protect sex-based care and recognise biological reality.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses were told to 'broaden their mindset' after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male; Jennifer Melle’s case also shows how NHS staff can be pressured over pronouns and sex-based language.

**Who this hits:** This affects female patients who need intimate care, nurses using changing rooms, and NHS staff who are asked to say things they do not believe. It is not an abstract policy fight if you are a woman on a ward or a nurse facing disciplinary action.

**Angle:** Our line is that the NHS must put truth, safety and conscience before ideology. Viewers will see how professional bodies can resist lawful, common-sense guidance, and they can ask their local trust whether it is complying with the Supreme Court’s judgment on sex and protecting single-sex spaces.

**Opening line:** "Would your hospital protect a female ward if activists objected?"

**Title:** *BMA urged to accept reality on sex in the NHS*

### 3. ['That knowledge could save lives': Shefford and Stotfold MP campaigns for Sex Ed to be compulsory until 18](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Education · Biggleswade Today*

An MP is campaigning for sex education to be compulsory until the age of 18, arguing that older teenagers need continued teaching on relationships, consent and safety.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Kristie Higgs lost her job after raising concerns about relationships and sex education, and Izzy Montague challenged LGBT teaching to very young children with no meaningful parental opt-out.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents of teenagers in sixth forms and colleges, not just parents of primary school children. It also affects Christian pupils who may be taught contested moral and sexual ideas as if they are unquestionable facts.

**Angle:** We should not sound as though parents want children kept ignorant; the issue is who decides the moral framework and whether parents are told the truth about what is being taught. Viewers will know to ask schools for lesson materials, consultation details and whether faith-based objections will be respected.

**Opening line:** "Should sex education really be compulsory until your child turns 18?"

**Title:** *Compulsory sex education to 18? Parents need answers*

### 4. [Archbishop of Liverpool condemns Manx Bill for Assisted Dying](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxPT3A2bGF1Q3Q2NzBUaE1TMFAyWngzcVJBOHgycUVKYzVmMUJibjE3cUlMWkR3SjlRSlBTaE5mZjRFRzZzcUdiR1pUcm55dUp3YUNqRlRGdEstQzNFMjdCeV96bmRKTWhTMkZ2OUlfMHZkVlNhY3pJMTdaWkUwSzYzbFVNUTZmZWZtWC1CSEtiTGNZSXVGaWVjZ2htbw?oc=5)
*End of life · The Tablet*

The Archbishop of Liverpool has condemned the Isle of Man’s Assisted Dying Bill, warning against changing the law to allow doctors to help patients end their lives.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Indi Gregory, Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Rashid Abbasi’s cases show why end-of-life law matters: vulnerable patients and families can be overruled when medical systems decide continued life is not in a patient’s best interests.

**Who this hits:** This affects elderly people, disabled people and seriously ill patients who may already feel they are a burden. It also affects families who want care, pain relief and time together, not a system that quietly offers death as a solution.

**Angle:** Our line is that assisted suicide changes the culture of medicine from caring to killing, especially where palliative care is under pressure. Viewers will understand that the question is not only individual choice, but whether vulnerable people will feel subtle pressure when they most need protection.

**Opening line:** "What happens when death becomes one of the treatment options?"

**Title:** *Archbishop warns against assisted dying law*

### 5. *Beginning of life · Right To Life UK*

Right To Life UK has marked the 59th anniversary of the Abortion Act receiving royal assent, stating that 11,256,470 lives have been lost since 1967.

**Who this hits:** This affects mothers facing crisis pregnancies, fathers who feel powerless, and unborn children whose lives are treated as disposable. It also affects churches that want to offer practical support but may not know where to start.

**Angle:** We should use the anniversary to remind viewers that abortion is not just a political argument but millions of missing lives and countless wounded families. Viewers should be encouraged to support pregnancy help, speak compassionately about abortion, and ask MPs to oppose any further liberalisation of the law.

**Opening line:** "Eleven million lives later, can Britain still call this healthcare?"

**Title:** *59 years of the Abortion Act: 11 million lives lost*

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [NHS trust humiliated as it finally updates trans-friendly changing room policy](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Gender · Daily Express*

An NHS trust has finally updated a trans-friendly changing-room policy after pressure over single-sex spaces. The story matters because it turns the Supreme Court and EHRC debate into a real workplace policy affecting nurses on shift.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses were told to 'broaden their mindset' after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; this is exactly the kind of NHS policy battle they faced.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, healthcare assistants and other NHS staff who have to get changed at work before and after a shift. It also affects female patients who want to know whether hospitals are taking biological sex and privacy seriously.

**Angle:** Our line is that this is not an abstract culture-war argument: it is about whether women can undress at work without being forced to share intimate spaces with men. Viewers will understand what the Supreme Court judgment means in practice, and why they should ask their own employers or NHS trusts whether policies have actually been updated.

**Opening line:** "Would you change for work beside a male colleague because HR said so?"

**Title:** *NHS changes trans changing-room policy after nurses object*

### 2. [Former UK Prime Minister Listed As ‘Core Participant’ in Grooming Gang Inquiry](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiywFBVV95cUxNSFZ4N016VFotVGRwR05aNFlvemh1VUlfSHZTZF9GNzZBdFZaeENmNU4wdWlpeDlvZVBDUkVubF9iVTRqeWlCX3Y4YldYeHktT1NkMjhHNmNiM2VnX19fS2xOT2gtRzRnenBHVFlJeDB1dnZQQlJCdXpGaEIwQ0J0NWRkWlUxQl91eE1QenJocmRseS1kMjQtbGpHZ1dQNHBNNXRDVXNNLWp0elNUSGUwcF8wUFUtV1I2ZmVXbDVXS1RfVUpKZlFnblVtdw?oc=5)
*Islam · PJ Media*

A former UK Prime Minister has reportedly been listed as a core participant in the grooming gang inquiry. Core participant status gives a person or organisation a formal role in the inquiry process, keeping attention on what senior figures and institutions knew or failed to do.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** 'Sarah' was groomed, raped, forced into sharia marriages, forcibly converted to Islam and subjected to forced abortions; her story shows exactly why these inquiries must not be allowed to become a whitewash.

**Who this hits:** This affects survivors who have waited years to be believed, and parents who want to know whether police, councils and politicians will protect children without fear of being called racist or Islamophobic.

**Angle:** Our line is that grooming gang inquiries must follow the evidence wherever it leads, including failures linked to religion, culture, police cowardice and social services. Viewers will understand why labels like 'Islamophobia' must never be used to silence victims, and why survivors need truth rather than managed apologies.

**Opening line:** "What did leaders know while girls were being groomed?"

**Title:** *Grooming gang inquiry: why survivors need truth, not excuses*

### 3. [Disability charity apologises for dropping choir over founder’s gender-critical beliefs](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Gender · Third Sector*

A disability charity has apologised after dropping a choir because of its founder’s gender-critical beliefs. The apology is significant because it recognises that excluding people for believing biological sex is real can be challenged.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Victoria Culf was cancelled and reported to the police for saying it is harmful for children to try to change their sex; this story shows the same pattern of gender-critical views being treated as beyond the pale.

**Who this hits:** This affects volunteers, choir members, charity workers and trustees who may privately believe that sex is real but fear being excluded from public life. It also affects disabled people who should not lose services or community activities because activists object to someone’s lawful beliefs.

**Angle:** Our line is that people should not be made untouchable for holding ordinary, lawful beliefs about sex. Viewers will see that apologies and climbdowns are possible, and that cancellation should be challenged calmly, firmly and in writing.

**Opening line:** "Can a charity drop a choir because one person believes sex is real?"

**Title:** *Charity apologises after cancelling choir over gender-critical beliefs*

### 4. [Oxford University students aim to CANCEL anti-woke academic who accused Jason Arday of plagiarism](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxORVBqMnNRWV9sZzBERTVKYlEydDdHbGpyTDNZNWwycHp2Z1JzM3FUQjNjQ3l4NG5NYXBMQ1pxWUNPVmVzU0lGQ1hIZmxnN3BOS2taRHR2UjlMeXBWZm14TE4xRm9ub2wwMGlxN2lXalp1WWFlNVlQbW9icTFEOGRxYW4yX2ctME9zTkdOWU1fT2hmVkg0Y0JTWW1PQQ?oc=5)

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Felix Ngole was expelled from a social work course over biblical views on marriage, and Aaron Edwards was sacked from a theology post over a tweet on sexuality; both show how academic spaces can punish unfashionable speech.

**Who this hits:** This affects Christian students, lecturers and parents sending children to university who wonder whether dissenting views can still be spoken aloud. It also affects anyone who expects universities to test arguments rather than silence unpopular people.

**Angle:** Our line is that universities should be places where serious claims are examined, not places where campaigns decide who is allowed to speak. Viewers will understand why free speech protections matter even when speech is sharp, uncomfortable or controversial.

**Title:** *Oxford cancellation row exposes free speech crisis on campus*

*Islam · Daily Mail*

Reports say a terrorist hate preacher used highly toxic social media rants aimed at children aged 11 to 15 on TikTok. The story raises urgent questions about real online radicalisation and how extremists reach children through ordinary platforms.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Our cases involving Indi Gregory, Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Rashid Abbasi show how vulnerable patients and families can already be overruled in life-and-death medical decisions.

**Angle:** Our line is that assisted suicide changes the whole culture of medicine, especially for those who feel like a burden. Viewers will see why safeguards often sound reassuring on paper but can fail in real hospitals, care homes and family situations.

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Church challenges Council's 'unprecedented' notice over public outreach](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxNdGNfYWxfcmFoeWpKRU42Q1NNRVYtblRiYmw1cEV5YkRvY1JQSGNMdGhmclVsTlgwaVBWX1R1ZDB5VjE1ZllYeDBtREZTVWNtRGQ5SmE3VnBzZXFZRXFqbnBzTWc4UW93bzVGSjNQSnpiWW44Wl85dDZtRmR3TnZjR3RQaGV2T1VRTU9xZGc2b0FHV0pSMmVvSFVVMlBPZHNxTHBXM3MyRlUxWWNuWTEtUnZBSHNWUQ?oc=5)
*Christian Concern in the news · Premier Christian News*

Premier reports that Bread of Life Community Church is challenging a council notice seeking to control its public evangelism. The notice reportedly goes beyond noise or obstruction and attempts to regulate the content of what Christians may say in public outreach.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bread of Life Community Church is our client: the council issued a Community Protection Notice seeking to control the content of its street evangelism.

**Who this hits:** This affects churches, street preachers and ordinary Christians who share the gospel in town centres, on high streets or outside events. If councils can dictate the content of evangelism, public Christian witness becomes something officials permit rather than a freedom Christians already have.

**Angle:** Our line is that councils must not use anti-social behaviour powers as a back-door blasphemy or censorship code. Viewers will understand that this is not just about one church, but about whether local authorities can decide which parts of the Christian message are acceptable in public. Churches should know that they can challenge overreaching notices rather than quietly stop evangelising.

**Opening line:** "Can a council tell a church what it is allowed to preach?"

**Title:** *Council notice challenged over attempt to control church evangelism*

### 2. [STATEMENT: NHS guidance on the provision of single-sex services and facilities](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxNVmQwQUhrRzhKc2RPSlZzYWtSRE1qNnRwRndFRjdCQmRVNjBhb0ZQQy00NG1qV21QUTZRNDliTXVLZFlJZWg3cVZySGZIUkRadjFoVlluenJ5aDg5dXcyYWY4YlU1QXdjVFlvUHNETUJGMDZ6dVh2dDhmUk11cFhCNnBSUVYtLWxGZXFaVlNTNTN3bF8tcXB2bFpBNmhMRUE5WW9CLXdNWmJtV3ZhSUpfUUM2R25vd0xP?oc=5)
*Gender · BMA*

The BMA has issued a statement on NHS guidance about single-sex services and facilities. The row is about whether NHS wards, changing rooms and intimate care should be organised around biological sex or gender identity.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses objected to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; Jennifer Melle also faces discipline after refusing compelled language around a male trans-identifying patient.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, doctors, hospital patients and families asking whether women-only spaces in the NHS really mean women-only. It is especially concrete for female staff changing at work and vulnerable patients receiving intimate care.

**Angle:** Our line is that after the Supreme Court judgment, public bodies and professional organisations cannot pretend biological sex is irrelevant. Viewers will see how guidance written in technical language can affect the ward, the changing room and the bedside. NHS staff should know they are not unreasonable for asking for sex-based privacy, dignity and safeguarding.

**Opening line:** "When the NHS says single-sex, does it actually mean biological sex?"

**Title:** *NHS single-sex guidance puts women’s privacy back in the spotlight*

### 3. [Sacked gender critical teacher 'could have shown respect'](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiXkFVX3lxTE5laXZtZjNUQXVadW1YYnBMTFZ1V25OZTcwa0xpaDZ5Wng1SkRaTkxHeXF5bmVTVnJVYnRBbzlpVnlQRTRlSzlQY2hFSnNkUkhvalpSNktoYmFpQUtSUkE?oc=5)
*Gender · BBC*

The BBC reports on a sacked gender-critical teacher, with the key issue framed as whether lawful beliefs were expressed with sufficient respect. The story again puts teachers’ beliefs about sex and gender under scrutiny inside schools.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Joshua Sutcliffe was disciplined for alleged misgendering and for his views on Islam; his case raises the same question of whether teachers can act according to Christian and biological convictions at work.

**Who this hits:** This affects teachers, classroom assistants and school staff who believe sex is real but fear one wrong phrase could cost them their job. It also matters for parents who want schools to be honest with children without punishing staff for dissenting from gender ideology.

**Angle:** Our line is that respect must not become a code word for compelled agreement. Viewers will understand the difference between treating every pupil with care and being forced to affirm claims about sex that Christians, and many others, believe are untrue. Teachers should be encouraged to seek clear policies and advice before being trapped by vague expectations.

**Opening line:** "Can a teacher lose their career for saying sex is real?"

**Title:** *Sacked teacher case shows the danger of compelled gender ideology*

### 4. [A UK teen made fun of a local politician. Then police showed up at his door.](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqAFBVV95cUxQNDE0NzZUOGVOcE5RRHdfZGZwb2RiWU1xcUpia3JFSXUtN052dFQybVVpRmVRSW9KbFplb3hRRXlKTzAxSUVaSmtqYmlpWEpDNy1ZUFBpZzhqUV9oSTdtVk5RUVFUQ0M3RzVQQTN0STN3X0FYRXphMXY1T2lhcE4tNHdSeXpkLWdxTE9uVTRfQWkwRmhPaExlRkZVcDdxVVdtV1FoQjljT1c?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · New York Post*

The New York Post reports that police visited a UK teenager after he mocked a local politician online. The story has gained attention because it shows police attention being directed at speech that appears rude or satirical rather than criminal.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Anthony Stevens was arrested in front of his family over a handful of tweets defending free speech; this story reflects the same pattern of police treating online speech as a policing matter.

**Who this hits:** This affects teenagers, parents and anyone who posts jokes, criticism or political comments online. A family could find officers at the door over words that should have been answered by debate, not police involvement.

**Angle:** Our line is that Britain is normalising police visits for speech that should never meet a criminal threshold. Viewers will understand why non-crime hate incidents and informal police warnings can chill speech even when no one is charged. Parents should know to ask calmly what law is alleged to have been broken and whether anything is being recorded against their child.

**Opening line:** "Should police turn up because a teenager mocked a politician?"

**Title:** *Police visit to teen over political mockery raises free speech alarm*

### 5. [The Conversion Practices Bill is weaponised vagueness](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikwFBVV95cUxQTE5Wb2Y3UTlUZXplZDhBVHZVRWNqY25JN2NwTUd6cEFVdGVPSkxVSkNFX0ZuWGFCejUwSHJQdnNraUtFck5aMTVBMWFWdm1kcGNZZHlqYmN2b0ZfVHpxcWh5ZHo1aU1rQ1JZdjZCd0hrUjRES2dtMWVVMk9Dd2VrWUhLanBFb1FIM0NoRV9uWkZQYTQ?oc=5)
*Sexuality · www.christiantoday.com*

Christian Today warns that a proposed Conversion Practices Bill is drafted so broadly that ordinary conversations, prayer and pastoral care could be caught. The concern is not coercion, but vague law being used against consensual Christian ministry.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Matthew Grech is being prosecuted in Malta for sharing his testimony of finding faith and leaving a homosexual lifestyle; his case shows how conversion practice laws can criminalise speech and testimony.

**Who this hits:** This affects pastors, youth leaders, parents and Christians who pray with someone asking for help with sexuality or identity. If the law is vague, people may stop having honest pastoral conversations because they fear being accused of illegal conversion practice.

**Angle:** Our line is that abuse and coercion should already be dealt with, but the state must not criminalise prayer, repentance, testimony or voluntary pastoral support. Viewers will understand why wording matters: a badly drafted law can punish the very conversations people freely seek from their church. Christians should ask MPs and churches whether the Bill clearly protects prayer, preaching and consensual pastoral care.

**Opening line:** "Could praying with someone become evidence of a crime?"

**Title:** *Conversion Practices Bill risks criminalising ordinary Christian pastoral care*

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Church challenges Council's 'unprecedented' notice over public outreach](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxNdGNfYWxfcmFoeWpKRU42Q1NNRVYtblRiYmw1cEV5YkRvY1JQSGNMdGhmclVsTlgwaVBWX1R1ZDB5VjE1ZllYeDBtREZTVWNtRGQ5SmE3VnBzZXFZRXFqbnBzTWc4UW93bzVGSjNQSnpiWW44Wl85dDZtRmR3TnZjR3RQaGV2T1VRTU9xZGc2b0FHV0pSMmVvSFVVMlBPZHNxTHBXM3MyRlUxWWNuWTEtUnZBSHNWUQ?oc=5)
*Christian Concern in the news · Premier Christian News*

Bread of Life Community Church is challenging a council notice that seeks to control its public Christian outreach. The case raises whether local authorities can police the content of peaceful evangelism in public spaces.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bread of Life Community Church is our client; the council notice directly targets the church's street evangelism and public Christian witness.

**Who this hits:** This affects any church that sings, preaches, offers prayer or hands out leaflets in a town centre. If a council can dictate what a church may say outdoors, ordinary evangelism becomes something Christians need official permission to do.

**Angle:** Our line is that councils must not become theological censors. Viewers will see how powers meant for nuisance and public order can be stretched into control of Christian speech, and why churches should know their rights before accepting restrictions on outreach.

**Opening line:** "Can a council tell a church what it is allowed to preach?"

**Title:** *Council Notice Challenged Over Church Street Evangelism*

### 2. [Conservative MS says Supreme Court ruling on sex is “crystal clear”](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqwFBVV95cUxQbFdaaWFZeVd2TTcyUTYtSWxHR3ZMVlNOQ3o5ZWcwR3BMTVZROFp3a3VOemY4a1VqYnRYR2UteWlQNkozUkZxZnF3Y0lmb1E0YnBwWWQydmZGUEh4WjF3U3ZMbGFmQXROd0gtZUU3ZEdrQVlFSWNIanYzOE5tZFNzemZXRnZXc1U4RWZXNUtGUXEtcGdIY3ZrNlBmUEl1aUtwVjM2RDZ5cnY1Njg?oc=5)
*Gender · Caerphilly Observer*

A Welsh Conservative Member of the Senedd has said the Supreme Court's ruling on the meaning of sex is “crystal clear”. The story keeps pressure on public bodies to apply the judgment in real policies, not just acknowledge it in words.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses were told to accept sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; their case shows why the Supreme Court ruling matters in everyday workplaces.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, teachers, council workers and service users who need clarity over single-sex spaces. It also affects women asking whether changing rooms, wards and toilets will be organised by biological sex or by self-identification.

**Angle:** Our line is that the law must now be followed in practice. Viewers will understand that the Supreme Court judgment is not an abstract culture-war point: it should shape workplace policies, NHS spaces and public services now.

**Opening line:** "If the law on sex is clear, why are women still being ignored?"

**Title:** *Supreme Court Sex Ruling: Public Bodies Must Now Comply*

### 3. [Euthanizing a Toddler Is Not Compassionate](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMie0FVX3lxTE9rcVlrbEVpTDlVNXU2U1lLem9rSC1FRnkxR19MTjd0M1AyQXJlRDd2WXJvcUdXdG5pRzFiMkpaOUVyRXFFWXRqTTJxLXVnbHN3eUdfcnhPSWJPQjZwX0ZiajN0T1Z4ZmZIanNxNGczVHRFQTRZRUVvUVltZw?oc=5)
*End of life · Christianity Today*

Christianity Today has published a warning against the euthanasia of a toddler, arguing that killing a child cannot be called compassion. The story highlights how end-of-life arguments can move from adults to the youngest and most vulnerable.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Indi Gregory was a baby whose life support was ordered withdrawn despite an offer of further treatment in Italy; her case shows how vulnerable children can be denied the presumption of life.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents of seriously ill children and families who fear doctors or courts may decide that a child's life is no longer worth sustaining. It also matters to grandparents and carers worried about where assisted dying arguments lead.

**Angle:** Our line is that compassion means care, pain relief and protection, not deliberately ending a child's life. Viewers will understand why debates about assisted suicide are not confined to rare adult cases: once law accepts some lives may be ended, the pressure falls on those least able to speak.

**Opening line:** "When did killing a sick toddler become something called compassion?"

**Title:** *Toddler Euthanasia Shows Where Assisted Dying Logic Leads*

### 4. [New Zealand’s High Court rules puberty blocker ban for trans youth is unlawful](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxNcmRyY0ptUEFvSTN2NFE5OUtrQ0FmTDh5VE5HdDBEOXVUVHdiMXV5dnJWUTM2ZkZGcGZ1WEFXa0ZuQThWTjM1MFZkTzJRMDgtczdfQkwyNDRoWXE3dVp3T2k5Slc2SW5XaDJLWFVwZEdOV1FUZUtWVmtGMHhaRUlEN1hjaFRPR2dLMnJzbGxWQjBzbjFXcmlYb0RKWnBZaFU?oc=5)
*Gender · attitude.co.uk*

New Zealand's High Court has ruled that a ban on puberty blockers for trans-identifying young people was unlawful. The judgment comes amid continuing international controversy over youth gender medicine and the evidence for such treatments.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Victoria Culf was cancelled and reported to police for saying it is harmful for children to try to change their sex; this story concerns the same safeguarding warning about medicalising distressed children.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents whose children are struggling with gender distress and are being offered medical pathways they may not fully understand. It also affects teachers and youth workers asked to affirm a pathway that can lead to powerful drugs.

**Angle:** Our line is that children's bodies must not be used in ideological experiments. Viewers will understand why the Cass Review matters in the UK, why parents should ask hard questions about evidence and risk, and why courts should not silence safeguarding concerns.

**Opening line:** "Would you let a court overrule safeguards on puberty blockers?"

**Title:** *Court Ruling Reopens Puberty Blocker Safeguarding Fears*

### 5. [PM backs ‘rigorous process’ behind Palestine Action ban after Rooney book halt](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · Belfast Telegraph*

The Prime Minister has defended the process behind the ban on Palestine Action after a Sally Rooney book event or publication was halted over concerns connected to the proscription. The story raises questions about how anti-terror laws affect speech, publishing and association beyond the group directly targeted.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bernard Randall was reported to Prevent, the government's terrorism watchdog, over a school sermon; his case shows how extremism frameworks can chill lawful speech when drawn or applied too broadly.

**Who this hits:** This affects authors, venues, publishers, students and ordinary people worried that lawful opinions could be treated as extremism by association. Christians should care even when they disagree with the speech involved, because the same tools can later be used against biblical beliefs.

**Angle:** Our line is that genuine violence and terrorism must be dealt with firmly, but free speech must not become collateral damage. Viewers will understand the difference between prosecuting crime and letting broad extremism powers frighten people into silence.

**Opening line:** "Can anti-terror law end up censoring books and lawful speech?"

**Title:** *Palestine Action Ban Sparks Wider Free Speech Questions*

### 1. [‘The Gospel belongs on the streets’: UK church challenges council’s preaching ban](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqAFBVV95cUxPMmZFRXkweWF2MjV5UDhwMFVMR2hVX0FsLTVzWkJPTW5ic2ZfWXVlenhWaTNONmU3ZWpfamplblBPRkpUSXJhN1BkdDZxanBRZkQ0M0hzNmdKQW5fZEZCbER0ZkpHakE2b0ZScGRtcVFJNzBJWVhLcUdjNDhvemZvZHR6czh6MURpVV9CZkdIYy1RRmtuNUpoTzRmOERRSjBmX0x2M0JVZl8?oc=5)
*Christian Concern in the news · Christian Post*

The Christian Post reports on a UK church challenging a council action that restricts its street preaching. The dispute is about whether a local authority can control the content of Christian evangelism in a public place.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bread of Life Community Church was issued with a Community Protection Notice seeking to control the content of its street evangelism; this is exactly the kind of council restriction the case challenges.

**Who this hits:** This affects churches, street preachers and ordinary Christians who share their faith in town centres. It also matters to anyone who assumes the gospel can still be spoken publicly without a council deciding which parts are acceptable.

**Angle:** Our line is simple: public authorities should not use anti-social behaviour powers to edit Christian preaching. Viewers will understand how ordinary evangelism can be reframed as a public-order problem, and why churches should know their rights before agreeing to council restrictions.

**Opening line:** "Can a council decide which parts of the gospel may be preached outdoors?"

**Title:** *Council preaching ban: can the gospel still be spoken in public?*

### 2. *Christian Concern in the news · Premier Christian News*

Premier Christian News reports that a Christian teacher is suing a school after being dismissed for expressing a pro-life view. The case puts the spotlight on whether school staff can be punished for saying unborn life matters.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Kristie Higgs was sacked by a school over a private Facebook post about relationships and sex education; this is the same pattern of school staff losing work for expressing Christian moral beliefs.

**Who this hits:** This affects Christian teachers, teaching assistants and school staff who wonder whether they can speak honestly about abortion, family or sexuality. It also affects parents who want schools to tolerate Christian convictions, not treat them as professional misconduct.

**Angle:** We should say that a pro-life conviction is not extremism or hatred; it is a core Christian belief about human dignity. Viewers will gain a clear warning about workplace speech in schools, and a practical reason to document concerns, seek advice early and resist unlawful viewpoint discrimination.

**Opening line:** "Could a teacher lose her job for saying unborn children matter?"

**Title:** *Christian teacher takes school to court over pro-life dismissal*

### 3. *Gender · Exeter Today*

Royal Devon NHS trust is reviewing new NHS guidance on privacy and dignity. The issue comes amid national scrutiny of how hospitals protect single-sex spaces and biological-sex privacy.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses were told to ‘broaden their mindset’ after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; this story raises the same question for NHS trusts.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, patients and hospital visitors who need intimate care, changing facilities or wards where sex matters. Women in particular need to know whether their local NHS trust will protect privacy in practice, not just on paper.

**Angle:** Our line is that NHS trusts must apply the law honestly after the Supreme Court judgment on sex, not hide behind vague dignity language. Viewers will understand what to ask their hospital or employer: are single-sex spaces based on biological sex, and what happens when staff object?

**Opening line:** "Will your hospital changing room follow biology, or ideology?"

**Title:** *NHS trust reviews privacy rules after sex-based rights row*

*Freedom of speech · UnHerd*

UnHerd reports that the UK terror watchdog has warned that ‘free speech absolutism’ can undermine democracy. The comment matters because terrorism and extremism language is increasingly being used in debates about lawful speech.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bernard Randall was dismissed and reported to Prevent over a school sermon telling pupils they did not have to accept LGBT ideology; Aaron Edwards was threatened with a counter-terrorism referral over a tweet on human sexuality.

**Who this hits:** This affects chaplains, teachers, lecturers and employees who hold orthodox Christian views and fear being labelled dangerous for saying so. It also affects parents whose children are in schools where disagreement can be treated as a safeguarding or extremism issue.

**Angle:** We should warn that democracy is not protected by treating peaceful Christian speech as a security risk. Viewers will see why vague extremism definitions matter in everyday life, and why MPs and schools must be challenged when Prevent-style language is used against lawful belief.

**Opening line:** "When did a school sermon become a terror concern?"

**Title:** *Terror watchdog warning raises free speech fears for Christians*

### 5. [How schools are indoctrinating your kids](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxPOXUxSV9fSWJrMGlDMDJDbkZqQmVWVW8talJtVWhYbHB2ZTcySlJHQ3JQSGtob05Tal9JVDVwX0YyYTFzck9KNU5tVFRqeE84LWFlSE9OWHBsTTk5dTA1UHhnOEt2bmFkWjE1Z2wteVJpUHJqSklSQXN0eFA1RzhYelNIMWptT3l2OGc?oc=5)
*Education · Spiked*

Spiked has published a high-profile piece arguing that schools are indoctrinating children rather than simply educating them. The story focuses attention on what pupils are being taught about identity, sexuality and ideology.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Izzy Montague challenged LGBT teaching to primary-aged children with no meaningful opt-out; Kristie Higgs lost her school job after raising concerns about RSE on Facebook; Bernard Randall was punished after a sermon on identity politics.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents choosing schools, parents with children in RSE lessons, and Christian pupils being taught that biblical beliefs are harmful or outdated. It is especially relevant to families who only discover lesson content after their child comes home upset or confused.

**Angle:** Our line is that parents, not the state, have primary responsibility for children’s moral formation. Viewers will get practical next steps: ask for RSE materials, check the school’s equality and trans policies, and object early when ideology is presented as fact.

**Opening line:** "Do you know what your child’s school is teaching about sex and identity?"

**Title:** *Are schools educating children, or pushing ideology?*

### 1. *Christian Concern in the news · Premier Christian News*

A Christian teacher is suing after allegedly being dismissed for expressing a pro-life view. The case puts the spotlight on whether teachers can hold and express mainstream Christian beliefs without losing their livelihood.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Kristie Higgs was sacked by a school over a private Facebook post raising concerns about relationships and sex education; this story shows the same pattern of school staff being punished for Christian moral beliefs.

**Who this hits:** This affects Christian teachers, teaching assistants and school staff who wonder whether one comment on abortion, marriage or sex education could cost them their job. It also affects parents who want schools to tolerate Christian views rather than treat them as dangerous.

**Angle:** We should make this a human story about conscience at work: if pro-life belief is treated as unfit for the classroom, many ordinary Christians are at risk. Viewers should come away knowing that employment law does protect Christian belief, and that they should not assume a school’s HR policy is the final word.

**Opening line:** "Can a teacher lose their job simply for being pro-life?"

**Title:** *Christian teacher takes school to court over pro-life dismissal*

### 2. [NHS England assessment warns new single-sex ward guidance could harm trans patients](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilwFBVV95cUxNMGF6STM1Q1V0ODZFZEExYkN0RXVNbmFvUFIzR2xmZUFPby0tZFJQVFZNTG1yeXBwSUZmeHZ5R3ZlZUc3SG13c2xZMmFEaTRsckFsajlOQXlNRFBBdnhTa0J4NVkwb0lrQUJzdVhydkRZMEM1YTVrOWlmTzNBTWhUQk9vTHB2VkNHeF9ZQURkNHB3Vzlud2Mw?oc=5)
*Gender · attitude.co.uk*

NHS England’s assessment reportedly warns that new single-sex ward guidance could harm trans patients. The issue comes after the Supreme Court clarified that sex in the Equality Act means biological sex, raising urgent questions about how NHS trusts protect women’s privacy and dignity.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses objected to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; this is the same real-world clash between gender identity policies and women’s single-sex spaces.

**Who this hits:** This affects female patients on hospital wards, elderly women needing intimate care, and nurses expected to follow policies that may ignore biological sex. It also affects NHS staff who are unsure whether they can speak up without being disciplined.

**Angle:** Our line should be clear: compassion for everyone cannot mean pretending sex is irrelevant in wards, changing rooms and intimate care. Viewers will understand what the Supreme Court judgment means in practice, and why they should ask their local NHS trust how it is protecting single-sex spaces.

**Opening line:** "Would your mother’s hospital ward be single-sex in reality, or only on paper?"

**Title:** *NHS single-sex wards: will women’s privacy survive gender policy?*

### 3. *Freedom of speech · UnHerd*

The UK’s terror watchdog has argued that “free speech absolutism” can undermine democracy. That language matters because counter-extremism and terrorism frameworks have already been used against peaceful Christian speech.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bernard Randall was dismissed and reported to Prevent after a school sermon telling pupils they did not have to accept LGBT ideology; Aaron Edwards was threatened with a counter-terrorism referral over a tweet on human sexuality.

**Who this hits:** This affects school chaplains, teachers, clergy, students and employees who express unfashionable Christian beliefs. It also affects parents whose children may be taught that orthodox Christian views are a safeguarding or extremism concern.

**Angle:** We should warn that vague language about extremism can quickly reach sermons, tweets and classroom conversations. Viewers will see why free speech is not a luxury for radicals, but a protection for ordinary Christians, and why they should challenge Prevent-style overreach in schools and workplaces.

**Opening line:** "When does a Christian sermon become an extremism concern?"

**Title:** *Terror watchdog warning raises fears for Christian free speech*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Anthony Stevens was arrested in front of his family over a handful of tweets defending free speech; his case shows how online speech policing can become a real knock at the door.

**Who this hits:** This affects anyone who posts political, religious or moral opinions online, including Christians sharing Bible verses or commenting on gender, Islam, abortion or sexuality. It especially affects small accounts that cannot fight a regulator or platform if they are wrongly flagged.

**Angle:** Our line should be that genuinely criminal content should be dealt with, but state-backed monitoring must not become a tool for silencing lawful Christian speech. Viewers will understand why online safety rules are not remote tech policy, but something that can affect what they are allowed to say from their own phone.

**Title:** *Ofcom, X and the growing policing of online speech*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses were told to ‘broaden their mindset’ after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; Jennifer Melle is also facing discipline over pronouns and a male trans-identifying patient.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, healthcare assistants and patients who need clear single-sex spaces in wards, changing rooms and intimate care. It also affects NHS staff who may be asked to use language or follow policies they believe are untrue or unsafe.

**Angle:** Our line is that compassion for trans-identifying people must not erase women’s privacy, staff conscience or biological reality. Viewers will understand what to ask their hospital trust or employer: does your policy follow the Supreme Court judgment, protect single-sex spaces, and respect staff who cannot affirm gender ideology?

**Opening line:** "Could your hospital policy make nurses choose between conscience and their job?"

**Who this hits:** This affects pastors, youth workers, parents and Christians who pray with someone asking for help with sexuality or gender distress. It also affects anyone who wants to say publicly that Jesus changed their life without being accused of causing harm.

**Angle:** Our line is that abuse is already wrong and should be punished, but vague ‘conversion practices’ bans can criminalise consensual Christian ministry. *Freedom of speech · World Israel News*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bernard Randall was dismissed and reported to Prevent over a school sermon telling pupils they did not have to accept LGBT ideology; Aaron Edwards was threatened with a counter-terror referral over a tweet on human sexuality.

**Who this hits:** This affects ordinary people who post strong political or religious opinions online and then find themselves treated like a security risk. It also affects teachers, chaplains and public-sector workers who may self-censor because a complaint could trigger an extremism process.

**Angle:** Our line is that counter-terror powers must be for genuine threats, not unpopular opinions. Viewers will understand the wider pattern: once ‘extremism’ becomes vague, Christians and others can be dragged into systems designed for terrorists simply for saying unfashionable things.

**Opening line:** "When does a political opinion become a counter-terror matter?"

**Title:** *Counter-terror police and online opinions: a warning for Christians*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses’ case shows why this matters: women were told to ‘broaden their mindset’ after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male.

**Who this hits:** This affects women using changing rooms, hospital wards, refuges, toilets and other single-sex services. It also affects employers and public bodies deciding whether they will follow the law or keep policies based on gender self-identification.

**Angle:** We should frame this as an attempt to relitigate clarity that women and public bodies urgently need. Viewers will understand that court challenges may not change anything immediately, but they can ask councils, hospitals, schools and employers whether their policies now reflect biological sex.

**Opening line:** "The Supreme Court gave clarity on sex. Will public bodies follow it?"

**Title:** *EHRC Guidance Challenged: The Fight Over Single-Sex Spaces Continues*

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Church takes on council over street preaching ban](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxQTFFzM1h4VEpzV09aeDVDTHhXQUtKOTRmbFdTM0E5NC1ZQUJsU1JLX05sTWM3QkpUMjg0Mmo5UkxIZWM3bmh6cXdpNldFM1E5dEdIRGRNZng2YTlOZHJwbHJQLXVMUm15VDNTV3RIZnRfdE1kallqRTdCM0lPX3U3STZ1WjdSSW1M?oc=5)
*Christian freedoms · The Telegraph*

A church is challenging a council after being served with a notice seeking to restrict what its evangelists can say in public. The dispute goes to the heart of whether councils can police the content of Christian preaching on the streets.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bread of Life Community Church is our case: the church was issued with a Community Protection Notice seeking to control the content of its street evangelism.

**Who this hits:** This affects street preachers, church outreach teams and ordinary Christians who hand out leaflets or speak about the gospel in town centres. If councils can dictate the content of preaching, public evangelism becomes permission-based.

**Angle:** We should say this is not about noise or obstruction, but about whether a council can decide which parts of Christianity may be spoken aloud. Viewers will understand that public preaching still has legal protection, and that churches should not quietly accept vague orders telling them to change their message.

**Opening line:** "Can a council tell a church which parts of the gospel it may preach?"

**Title:** *Church challenges council over street preaching restrictions*

### 2. [Trans people should use hospital spaces according to biological sex, NHS England says](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiXkFVX3lxTFBKbnYwZzJ0UFpNNGRvUEx0eGxwYkRQekk4MmtRYUJFWno2RkxJNFd5YnlZR0RxYzRtR3JlMHFlX0xwTFdETzF6akJmTTF1U2pyY2R0NTZZbWNjQjNaVXc?oc=5)

### 1. [Bread of Life Community Church challenging council order restricting street preaching in Colchester](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Christian Concern in the news · ITVX*

ITVX reports that Bread of Life Community Church is challenging a council order in Colchester that seeks to restrict how its members preach in public. The case raises whether a local authority can control the content of Christian evangelism on the street.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bread of Life Community Church is our client: it was issued with a Community Protection Notice seeking to control the content of its street evangelism.

**Who this hits:** This affects Christians who share their faith in town centres, outside churches, or in ordinary public spaces. It also affects anyone who assumes peaceful preaching is still lawful unless it is genuinely abusive or obstructive.

**Angle:** Our line is that councils must not use public order powers as a back-door licensing scheme for the gospel. Viewers will understand how ordinary evangelism can be rebranded as a nuisance, and why Christians should know their rights before they are challenged by officials or police.

**Opening line:** "Can a council tell a church what it is allowed to preach?"

**Title:** *Council order challenged over restrictions on Christian street preaching*

**Angle:** Our line is that the state should punish harassment, not peaceful prayer or offers of help. Viewers will learn why buffer zones are not just about stopping intimidation, but can be used to silence a Christian presence altogether.

**Who this hits:** This affects Christians, ex-Muslims, journalists and anyone who wants to discuss religion honestly. In Britain the danger is not a death sentence, but police, employers or regulators treating legitimate criticism of Islam as forbidden speech.

**Angle:** We should be clear that no one should be threatened or abused, but no religion should be protected from criticism by law. Viewers will understand the difference between protecting Muslims from hatred and creating a blasphemy code by the back door.

**Opening line:** "A woman may die for a post about Muhammad. Why should Britain care?"

**Title:** *Iran Blasphemy Death Sentence: A Warning Against Policing Religious Criticism*

**Who this hits:** This affects ordinary Christians who share their faith in town centres, hand out tracts, sing hymns, or answer questions in public. If councils can dictate the content of evangelism, street preaching becomes a permission-based activity.

**Angle:** We should say plainly that peaceful Christian witness is not anti-social behaviour. Viewers will understand how local powers such as Community Protection Notices can be used to censor religious speech, and they can support the church by signing or sharing the petition and watching what their own councils are doing.

### 1. [Petition to be delivered to Colchester City Council over criminalising church’s street preaching](https://christianconcern.com/ccpressreleases/petition-to-be-delivered-to-colchester-city-council-over-criminalising-churchs-street-preaching/)
*Christian Concern in the news · Christian Legal Centre*

Supporters of Bread of Life Community Church are due to gather at Colchester City Council on Wednesday 14 October to deliver a petition to chief executive Pamela Donnelly. The church is challenging a Community Protection Notice which seeks to control the content of its street evangelism.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Christian Legal Centre represents Bread of Life Community Church, which is facing council action over what it may say while preaching publicly.

**Who this hits:** This affects churches, evangelists and ordinary Christians who share their faith in town centres. If a council can dictate the content of one church’s preaching, other councils may try the same approach.

**Angle:** The line is simple: councils should not be licensing the gospel or deciding which parts of Christian preaching are acceptable. Viewers will understand how ordinary public order powers can be stretched into censorship, and they can support the petition or ask their own council how it treats street preaching.

**Opening line:** "Can a council decide what parts of the gospel may be preached?"

**Title:** *Colchester Council challenged over street preaching restrictions*

*Christian Concern in the news · www.christiantoday.com*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Christian Legal Centre represents Stephen Green, who was prosecuted for holding a Bible verse sign inside an abortion clinic buffer zone.

**Who this hits:** This affects anyone who prays, offers help, or quietly expresses pro-life beliefs near a clinic. It also matters for Christians who want to know whether quoting the Bible in public can now be treated as a criminal act.

**Angle:** We should say this is not about harassment; it is about whether peaceful, religious speech can be banned in a public place. Viewers will see why buffer zones are not a small technical change but a live threat to prayer, witness and help for vulnerable women.

*Freedom of speech · www.christiantoday.com*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Stephen Green’s case shows the same pattern in another setting: peaceful pro-life expression being pushed out of public spaces and treated as unacceptable.

**Who this hits:** This affects pro-life voters, party members, students and campaigners who expect to take part in democratic debate. If pro-life groups can be cancelled from party conferences, ordinary people may wonder whether they are welcome in politics at all.

**Angle:** Our line should be that abortion is a matter of life and death, so it must be debated openly rather than shut down. Viewers will understand that free speech is not only about courts and street preaching; it is also about whether political parties allow Christian and pro-life citizens into the room.

*End of life · The Christian Institute*

A group of celebrities has urged the Prime Minister to address the state of palliative care. The intervention comes amid continuing national pressure over assisted suicide and end-of-life policy.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Rashid Abbasi, Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Indi Gregory’s cases all show how vulnerable families can feel when medical systems move towards ending treatment rather than fighting for life.

**Who this hits:** This affects families with elderly parents, disabled relatives or seriously ill children who may soon need end-of-life care. It is also directly relevant to anyone worried that assisted suicide could be offered before proper care is available.

**Angle:** We should welcome the focus on palliative care while warning that Britain must not normalise assisted suicide as a shortcut for under-resourced care. Viewers should come away knowing to ask their MP a concrete question: will you fix palliative care before giving doctors power to help patients die?

**Opening line:** "Before politicians talk about assisted suicide, who is fixing care for the dying?"

**Title:** *Celebrities call for palliative care fix amid assisted suicide debate*

### 5. [Ministers have failed to act as extremist ideologies move into mainstream, warns Met chief](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Islam · Jewish News*

The Met chief has warned that ministers have failed to act as extremist ideologies move into the mainstream. The warning raises questions about whether public bodies are confronting real extremism while also protecting lawful speech.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Christian Legal Centre represents Luke Salmons, a police community support officer who was suspended and forced to resign after questioning Islam during mandatory diversity training.

**Who this hits:** This affects police officers, teachers, public-sector workers and church leaders who are told to take extremism seriously but may be punished for asking honest questions about ideology. It also affects communities worried about genuine extremism being ignored until it is too late.

**Angle:** Our line should be that the state must distinguish real extremism from lawful Christian belief and legitimate criticism of religion. Viewers will understand the double standard: public institutions can be quick to target Christians for speech, while senior police now warn that dangerous ideologies have been allowed to grow.

**Opening line:** "Why are Christians reported for speech while extremist ideologies go mainstream?"

**Title:** *Met warning exposes double standard on extremism and free speech*

Viewers should be encouraged to ask their local council what age-appropriate safeguards are in place for children’s events and displays.

**Opening line:** "Would you expect sex education material in your child’s local library?"

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Stephen Green was prosecuted for holding a Bible verse sign inside an abortion clinic buffer zone; both cases show pro-life speech being treated as something to be removed from public view.

**Who this hits:** This affects pro-life Christians, students, charities and party members who want to take part in public debate without being shouted down or disinvited. It also affects voters who expect political parties to hear arguments they may disagree with.

**Angle:** Our line should be that a democracy cannot claim to value women, babies or conscience while excluding one side of the abortion debate. Viewers should understand that cancellation is not just a campus problem; it is now reaching party politics and legal rights of participation.

**Title:** *Pro-Life Group Threatens Legal Action After SNP Cancellation*

**Angle:** We should welcome any pause, but warn that the campaign for assisted suicide will return. Viewers should use the breathing space to ask their MP to oppose assisted suicide and to back better hospice and palliative care instead.

A pastor is appealing after being convicted over a Bible message near an abortion clinic buffer zone. The case raises the question of whether quoting or preaching Scripture in a public place can now be treated as a criminal offence if it happens near a clinic.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Stephen Green was prosecuted for holding a sign with a Bible verse inside an abortion clinic buffer zone; this story goes to the same issue of Christian witness being criminalised near abortion facilities.

**Who this hits:** This affects street preachers, pro-life volunteers and ordinary Christians who pray or speak in public near abortion clinics. It also matters for church leaders who need to know whether pastoral or biblical speech can be restricted by local or national buffer zone rules.

**Angle:** We should say plainly that protecting women from harassment must not become a licence to ban the Bible from public space. Viewers will understand that buffer zones are not just about conduct, but increasingly about the content of Christian speech, and they should watch how councils and police apply these powers locally.

**Opening line:** "Can quoting the Bible near an abortion clinic now make you a criminal?"

**Title:** *Pastor appeals conviction over Bible sermon near abortion buffer zone*

**Who this hits:** This affects anyone who might stop, pray or offer quiet help near an abortion clinic, even without approaching anyone. It also affects pro-life church members who need to know whether silent prayer is being treated as suspicious or criminal.

**Angle:** Our line is that the state should not be policing thoughts or silent prayer. Viewers will see that this is not a theoretical free speech debate: real people are facing criminal charges for peaceful conduct, and Christians should ask their councils and MPs whether prayer is being banned in their area.

**Opening line:** "If silent prayer is a crime, what freedom is left?"

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Matthew Grech is being prosecuted in Malta for sharing his Christian testimony of leaving a homosexual lifestyle; his case shows how conversion therapy-style laws can criminalise speech and testimony.

**Who this hits:** This affects pastors, youth leaders, parents and Christians who pray with someone about sexuality or gender. If the law is badly drafted, ordinary conversations in a church office or family home could become legally risky.

**Angle:** We should argue that no one should be coerced, but consensual prayer and pastoral help must remain lawful. Viewers will understand the practical danger: a ban sold as stopping abuse can end up threatening parents, pastors and former LGBT people who simply tell their own story.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bernard Randall was reported to Prevent over a sermon on identity politics, and Luke Salmons was forced out after questioning Islam during diversity training; both show how official systems can be used against lawful Christian speech.

**Who this hits:** This affects teachers, chaplains, councillors, students and employees who worry that questioning Islam or ideology at work could be treated as extremism. If it can happen to a public figure, ordinary Christians will wonder what chance they have.

**Angle:** Our line is that criticism of Islam, like criticism of Christianity, must be protected in a free society. Viewers will see how Prevent and police reporting can be misused to chill lawful speech, and they should be alert if schools, councils or employers blur disagreement with extremism.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Simon Pearson lost his teaching job after being unfairly branded “Islamophobic”; his case shows how vague anti-Muslim hostility labels can damage real careers.

**Who this hits:** This affects teachers, councillors, church leaders and grooming gang survivors who need to speak honestly about Islam, sharia or abuse without being smeared. It also affects parents whose children may be taught under policies shaped by definitions they have never been allowed to see.

**Angle:** We should say that if a definition may restrict speech, the public must be allowed to see the evidence behind it. Viewers will understand why transparency matters: hidden consultations can become rules that govern what they may say at work, online or in public meetings.

**Opening line:** "Why won’t the public be allowed to see the Islamophobia evidence?"

**Title:** *Government secrecy over Islamophobia consultation raises free speech fears*

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Christian woman charged five times over silent prayer near abortion clinic](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivAFBVV95cUxQWkpGQWhoaS1MQlVhMHRyeFV2R2hiRDgzcnozRHMxY1FHbGtqR3hWcDlfM2oyVjV1dzRaS2RfS2RmTzFpVkVJTThpdjlOQzkxNTRBdXNIZU1xQ0kzOEp2S192eGZ3NHJJQXdhU19jdHRLTFM0cGozOEJLNklIZkE4STdhMjRDNUtIamdOMmxYWlFIcm1yS0tUNFJJOGs0Mk5lRUtSZm1STG9uMkpVWUxGRDYzWkVHVEtVREh1eg?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · Premier Christian News*

A Christian woman has reportedly been charged five times in relation to silent prayer near an abortion clinic. The case highlights how buffer-zone laws and local orders can treat quiet prayer or peaceful presence as a criminal matter.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** We represent Livia Tossici-Bolt, who is challenging a Bournemouth abortion clinic Public Space Protection Order that censors speech and makes prayer illegal; we also represent Stephen Green, prosecuted for holding a Bible verse sign inside a buffer zone.

**Who this hits:** This affects anyone who prays, offers help, or even stands silently near an abortion clinic. It also matters for pro-life volunteers who need to know whether ordinary peaceful witness could now lead to police action.

**Angle:** Our line is that the state should not be policing silent prayer. Viewers will understand how buffer zones move beyond preventing harassment and can become viewpoint censorship, and why they should ask their council and MP whether prayer, offers of help, and consensual conversation are being criminalised locally.

**Opening line:** "Can silent prayer really get you charged by the police in Britain?"

**Title:** *Christian Woman Charged Five Times Over Silent Prayer Near Abortion Clinic*

### 2. [Birmingham council leader vows action as grooming gangs inquiry begins](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinAFBVV95cUxPLWREXzlFeTNobFZDY3FjajFmMm5CMW9tS0tBSUhLNE9BcVdYVkR1MjY0MTByUjlWQlF3VEJvZ2s2cWJDMFlqaUFsRXJnMjZoNlhhS1d1T2p1amZFcnVPRFp5U3NacV9ORnlqT0lsNWpZZU1FNENSeFRoMkNtYnl0aV9TQmdIZ1pmbTYtVEZvaENZRi1GMk1jSEVNY3o?oc=5)
*Islam · https://www.birmingham-now.co.uk/*

Birmingham’s council leader has promised action as an inquiry into grooming gangs begins. The story raises urgent questions about whether victims will finally be heard and whether public bodies will confront abuse honestly.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** We represent 'Sarah', who was groomed, raped, forced into sharia marriages, forcibly converted to Islam, subjected to forced abortions, and then failed by police and social services.

**Who this hits:** This affects girls at risk now, survivors still waiting to be believed, and parents who expect police, schools and social services to protect children without fear or political embarrassment. It also affects communities where people have been afraid to speak plainly about grooming, coercion and religious control.

**Angle:** Our line is that any inquiry must put victims before reputational management. Viewers will understand why labels such as ‘racism’ or ‘Islamophobia’ must never be used to silence survivors, and why local authorities must be pressed on safeguarding, forced conversion, sharia marriage and institutional failure.

**Opening line:** "Will Birmingham finally listen to the girls nobody wanted to hear?"

**Title:** *Birmingham Grooming Gangs Inquiry: Will Victims Finally Be Heard?*

### 3. [Supreme Court rules against Colorado law banning 'conversion therapy' for minors](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi-?oc=5)
*Sexuality · ABC7 Los Angeles*

The US Supreme Court has ruled against a Colorado law banning so-called conversion therapy for minors. Although this is an American ruling, it matters in the UK because similar bans are repeatedly proposed here.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** We represent Matthew Grech, prosecuted in Malta for sharing his Christian testimony of leaving a homosexual lifestyle, showing how conversion-practices laws can criminalise speech, testimony and pastoral conversation.

**Who this hits:** This affects Christian parents, pastors, counsellors and young people who want freedom to talk and pray about sexuality or identity without the state treating that as abuse. In the UK, it is especially relevant wherever politicians promise a conversion therapy ban but refuse to protect ordinary prayer and pastoral care.

**Angle:** Our line is that no one should be coerced or abused, but consensual conversation, prayer and Christian teaching must remain lawful. Viewers will understand the difference between banning abuse and criminalising beliefs, and they can ask MPs for clear protections for parents, churches, counsellors and testimonies.

**Opening line:** "Could sharing your testimony one day be called conversion therapy?"

**Title:** *US Court Pushes Back on Conversion Therapy Ban — Why UK Christians Should Watch*

### 4. [Free speech battle erupts as Jenrick reported to police over warning to ‘eradicate’ radical Islam](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixwFBVV95cUxPM0NPdV9la3R2WFFULUMzcmRQWHVlWk85Y3VQXzFOM2M4dGE1MjlLUWVHM0xQNThRUGNZdTl1NDRFaEdIUnBvMDJ6dGxHRExJajlPbzdjdzZrdUR0N2dQYnNsY21BWVJ6X2pBZVVtQ3ZFUVZmalJrbExCOUZHVlV3TXhuVkhxbUtad29sTXlTdl9udXJIa1gtejc1ZE90VE42bDdhUTFZUDJlc0lhd01XTG5VaHg0ZVVtUExxdWotLUU1QUZrODlv?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · London Business News*

A free speech row has erupted after Robert Jenrick was reportedly referred to police over comments about ‘eradicating’ radical Islam. The dispute centres on whether strong criticism of an ideology can be treated as a policing matter.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** We represent John Steele, arrested and prosecuted for asking about the Qur'an’s teaching on domestic violence, and Shaun O’Sullivan, arrested after saying Christians worship a different God to Muslims.

**Who this hits:** This affects anyone who wants to discuss Islam, radicalism or religious teaching in public without fearing a police report. It especially matters for street preachers, teachers, councillors and ordinary Christians posting online.

**Angle:** Our line is that people must be protected from threats and violence, but criticism of religious ideas must remain free. Viewers will understand how blasphemy laws can return through the back door when police are asked to investigate robust political or religious speech, and why they should resist vague ‘anti-Muslim hostility’ definitions that chill legitimate debate.

**Opening line:** "When did criticising radical Islam become something to report to police?"

**Title:** *Jenrick Reported to Police: Free Speech or Blasphemy Law by the Back Door?*

### 5. [Assisted dying by the back door](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifkFVX3lxTE84aTF2WEMzNUt2OHRFdnVCbmxyYklXMkR4TW55ckZadzlzYWloWHVGcE9Xc3BjY3huT0FlRks0aXNoRlltY2RZNTlKVUJLUlFYOXg4Ui1IYnZSaHR1MFMtV3ZQWTVYNHZOeXFtZ09lYXdCd3REcE9FTlA4Z29LZw?oc=5)
*End of life · Spiked*

The article warns that assisted dying is being normalised without the public fully realising what is changing. It reflects the wider concern that end-of-life practice can shift before Parliament or the public have properly faced the consequences.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** We represented families including Indi Gregory’s, and supported cases such as Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Rashid Abbasi, where patients or parents fought hospitals and courts over life-sustaining treatment and the value of continuing care.

**Who this hits:** This affects elderly, disabled and seriously ill people, and families trying to protect a loved one in hospital. The practical fear is that a vulnerable patient could be steered towards death when what they need is care, pain relief, time and advocacy.

**Angle:** Our line is that Britain needs better palliative care, not a medical culture that makes death easier to offer than treatment and support. Viewers will understand why assisted suicide is not just about individual choice in extreme cases, but about pressure, safeguards, hospital culture and whether vulnerable people are treated as burdens.

**Opening line:** "What if assisted dying arrives before the law even says it can?"

**Title:** *Assisted Dying by the Back Door: Why Vulnerable Patients Are at Risk*

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Robert Jenrick MP reported to police and Prevent over comments on Islam](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxNRkJWS3VBYlk1M3ZTUTFwZmt4Y1ByV25FenM0ME1rTXpqTU02dWpTeExIRzFrVnlLVlVnYmgyWDVUTHhjaUt5b2tKUHRvTjQ3R08tS1ZQdlU4SENjQjJ6OEVGelBKOHRVYWpJNGxYNGRURmdNalNjVHJjcDdzNDgxSS1XNVVKNS03WDdqQ19feGpNME9nNmRVREdaTV9wb3VBaEo3NjlEeEpEZw?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · 5Pillars*

Robert Jenrick MP has reportedly been referred to both the police and Prevent over comments he made about Islam. The story raises the question of whether criticism of Islamic ideas is being treated as extremism or hate speech.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Luke Salmons was forced out of policing after questioning Islam during mandatory diversity training; Bernard Randall was reported to Prevent after a school sermon telling pupils they did not have to accept LGBT ideology.

**Who this hits:** This affects teachers, police officers, councillors, clergy and ordinary employees who may need to ask honest questions about religion or ideology at work. If an MP can be reported to Prevent for political speech, many Christians will wonder what would happen to them.

**Angle:** We should warn that Prevent must not become a tool for silencing lawful criticism of Islam or Christian moral teaching. Viewers will understand how extremism labels can be stretched far beyond terrorism, and why they should challenge vague workplace or school policies that treat disagreement as danger.

**Opening line:** "If an MP can be reported to Prevent, what happens to ordinary Christians?"

**Title:** *Robert Jenrick reported to Prevent: when criticism becomes ‘extremism’*

### 2. [Pastor Clive Johnston to appeal conviction for preaching John 3:16](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiogFBVV95cUxNZ01lRnJEOXVsOEhCbmhVa2lBdW1BdWFfMEZyRGlBZG5RblNSa1NmaUhQelZNY2xJVFlpRERnaHVnVkxWeTRTNFRyS3JxeHhwNGtCSWNTQ1hqdHJtQnF6MXJVN3lDT2x2YXd3UVB2d2FXc3BabktzWjM2RWdxekNMTkptVndaSUUzSWY3aFpnVTFMbFBqcXEyX3Ntd2UzS0dZaHc?oc=5)
*Christian freedoms · The Christian Institute*

Pastor Clive Johnston is appealing his conviction after preaching from John 3:16 in public. The case concerns whether ordinary Christian street preaching is being criminalised through public order law.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bread of Life Community Church was issued with a Community Protection Notice seeking to control the content of its street evangelism; Shaun O'Sullivan and John Steele also faced police action after public comments about Christianity and Islam.

**Who this hits:** This affects street preachers, churches running outreach, and Christians who share the gospel in public places. It also matters to anyone who expects the police and courts to distinguish between offensive abuse and lawful Christian proclamation.

**Angle:** Our line should be that preaching the most famous verse in the Bible must not be treated as a public order offence. Viewers will see that the issue is not only one pastor, but whether councils and police are making public Christian witness feel legally dangerous.

**Opening line:** "Can preaching John 3:16 now get you convicted?"

**Title:** *Pastor appeals conviction for preaching John 3:16*

### 3. [NI conversion practices Bill - what Christians need to know](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitAFBVV95cUxOZjhEdEJHeUV5aE5ZejRqVkxaeHJETEtOMnk0OXdTQkRwM1hhT0oxczZwRDJBdXNOWFpHb0FvUzNhWXV5dWlaYXZSRVhUQ01oZlJlODYwdEpoakdYUVV3Rm85bEc0Z3NVd2lhMFZNRjJPUFdxenVCc2xRUXIwN0ZJQUxvamJfNm5iNWlFeldVbkJraHg5TF9RdVdFbks5UkVNcXptajBYVnV1R0JpcTZmcUp0SGg?oc=5)
*Sexuality · Evangelical Focus*

A proposed conversion practices Bill in Northern Ireland is being scrutinised for its possible impact on prayer, pastoral care and Christian teaching on sexuality. Christians are being urged to understand what the Bill could criminalise or chill.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Matthew Grech was prosecuted in Malta for sharing his testimony of finding faith and leaving a homosexual lifestyle, showing how conversion therapy laws can be used against Christian testimony.

**Who this hits:** This affects pastors, youth leaders, parents and Christian counsellors who may be asked for prayer or advice by someone struggling with sexuality or identity. It could also affect church members who simply want to share how their faith changed their life.

**Angle:** We should argue that no law should criminalise coercion by banning consensual prayer, conversation or testimony. Viewers will learn the practical questions to ask: does the Bill protect ordinary pastoral care, parental guidance and the freedom to say that following Christ can transform every part of life?

**Opening line:** "Could a conversion therapy law criminalise prayer and testimony?"

**Title:** *Northern Ireland conversion practices Bill: what Christians must watch*

### 4. [Conservatives vow to keep ‘ideological brainwashing’ out of schools](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiogFBVV95cUxPUUVJQUVFa2hET1ZrOTJ0ck9Iek40QnhvNFh5YmpXUTJUeFBZRnA4M0YyUjE4bFYtWkxrM3N0TTR1STN3RDBwUjRxdWRMQ0hBY0NYLTNEbHUxUjQ0Y3BKZzBpemJYZnNwamVqNlNTYldDVGxrRWpOU3NFRUZfNkttVS1jTGV6cGNmeUdQbjc5NXZBeG12N0ZMUHdYN2l3T0p2aUE?oc=5)
*Education · The Christian Institute*

The Conservatives have pledged to keep what they call ‘ideological brainwashing’ out of schools. The debate focuses on what children are being taught about sex, gender and relationships, and whether parents are being kept properly informed.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Kristie Higgs lost her job after raising concerns online about relationships and sex education; Izzy Montague challenged a primary school after LGBT material was promoted to very young children with no opt-out.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents choosing schools, asking to see curriculum materials, or wondering what their children are being told about gender and sexuality. It also affects teachers who fear disciplinary action if they question lesson content.

**Angle:** We should welcome any serious move to remove gender ideology from classrooms, while pressing all politicians to protect parental rights in practice, not just in slogans. Viewers will know what to ask their school: what is being taught, by whom, at what age, and can parents see the materials?

**Opening line:** "Do you know what your child’s school is teaching about gender?"

**Title:** *Schools, gender ideology and the fight for parental rights*

### 5. [15-year-old schoolboy arrested for calling a Conservative councillor a "rent boy"](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipgFBVV95cUxORnptc0xDdlJtSUFrNjV1aWJNQjF6T0t3X0hhZXpqd3RxdHQ0Y09oREl1V3lTWHRZQUtkcjNwSGNGaUFwQVRXdDVRSXQzNERwRlN6c2tFT0pnX2xPeVBIZEgwcjUyRkhNMndvNGo5UXR5VmZSamR2OURUMkJORGM2c2ZxRlBvTjRyajBkeG51anpzRHNWZWYwTXJyOXFaSTJUdlhxSFN3?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · Free Speech Union*

A 15-year-old schoolboy was reportedly arrested after calling a Conservative councillor a ‘rent boy’. The story has prompted concern about whether police are using arrest powers proportionately in cases involving offensive speech.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Anthony Stevens was arrested in front of his family over tweets defending free speech; Victoria Culf was reported to police for saying it is harmful for children to try to change their sex.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents whose teenagers say foolish or offensive things online or in public, and adults who fear a police record for speech rather than real crime. It also affects councillors and public figures who should be able to challenge abuse without turning every insult into a policing matter.

**Angle:** We should say plainly that Christians need not defend crude insults in order to oppose disproportionate policing. Viewers will understand the difference between condemning nasty speech and allowing police powers to be used in ways that chill ordinary expression.

**Opening line:** "Should a teenager be arrested for an offensive insult?"

**Title:** *Teen arrested over insult: are police overreaching on speech?*
