# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Grooming gang inquiry to examine Birmingham](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxPVEJmd1RiclJPWTRoaUlhQUIzZmZINlRVLU5GODh3NFBnSTdRZ1gxdVdmRVhHT2cyZE0wcEVDQmNHbFBQTTRQZXZNcG1LMHdyanRNT19PMXpDWUtRdHRKcE5LZWxuNlVocTU4d29LTHVBM3dwb21ycDJhbGMtSDVFWi02dElKY2x3?oc=5)
*Islam · birminghamdispatch.co.uk*

Reports say the grooming gang inquiry will examine Birmingham, putting local police, social services and council responses under scrutiny. This widens the focus beyond individual offenders to whether institutions ignored warning signs or failed victims.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** 'Sarah' was groomed, repeatedly raped, forced into sharia marriages, forced to convert to Islam and subjected to forced abortions; her case shows exactly why inquiries must ask what police and social services knew and why victims were not protected.

**Who this hits:** This affects survivors who were dismissed or silenced, and parents worried that authorities still do not take grooming risks seriously. It also affects churches and community leaders who need courage to speak plainly when girls are being exploited.

**Angle:** Our line is that any inquiry must be fearless about ideology, ethnicity, religion and institutional cowardice. Viewers should understand that words like 'community cohesion' or 'Islamophobia' must never be used to bury abuse; they can press local councillors and MPs to demand full disclosure and survivor-led evidence.

**Opening line:** "What if the biggest scandal is not just the gangs, but who looked away?"

**Title:** *Birmingham grooming inquiry: will victims finally be heard?*

### 2. ['Can't wait to be arrested': John Cleese formally reported to UK's 'counter-terrorism' regime for criticizing Islam](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · Blaze Media*

John Cleese has reportedly been referred to the UK's counter-terrorism system after comments criticising Islam. Being reported is not the same as being arrested, but the use of counter-terror language against religious criticism is deeply alarming.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bernard Randall was reported to Prevent after a school sermon telling pupils they did not have to accept LGBT ideology; John Steele was arrested and prosecuted for asking about the Qur'an's teaching on domestic violence.

**Who this hits:** This affects teachers, chaplains, comedians, street preachers and ordinary workers who ask whether criticising a religion could get them flagged as extremist. It especially matters for Christians who want to speak honestly about Islam without police or Prevent consequences.

**Angle:** Our line is that Britain is drifting toward blasphemy by bureaucracy: not an official blasphemy law, but counter-terror, hate and safeguarding systems being used to chill lawful speech. Viewers gain a clear test: criticism of ideas, including religious ideas, must remain lawful even when it offends.

**Opening line:** "Since when did criticising a religion become a counter-terror matter?"

**Title:** *John Cleese and Prevent: is criticism of Islam being treated as extremism?*

### 3. [Human rights watchdog accuses trans activists of misinformation over single-sex space guidance](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxNQndaUVpqUzNTTHZIWTEtSGtVZzJubFg1VDlHSTVkUmc2bEtPZFN5QkJ6TUR1cEZDVEJxZG1GSGM2cEdQaV9WLVN2OGc4bTlyZElrLTJyLU9IVUxiQkROMHZYLWw5dm8wNVFmMm5jTkhNUkM1ZmI1SzhJNC1BR1U1U1ptcUpmZFlQREVkMElNbDVLZW1UcUhfVUhsS0xBODZmRXZ3?oc=5)
*Gender · GB News*

The human rights watchdog has accused trans activists of spreading misinformation about guidance on single-sex spaces. The dispute follows the Supreme Court ruling on the meaning of sex and raises the question of whether public bodies are applying the law honestly.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses were told to 'broaden their mindset' after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; their case is exactly about whether women can rely on single-sex spaces at work.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses changing before a shift, women using hospital wards or refuges, schoolgirls in toilets and changing rooms, and managers being told to rewrite policies. It is not abstract: it is about who can undress, receive care or work with dignity and privacy.

**Angle:** Our line is that the law must be followed, not reinterpreted by activist pressure. Viewers should know they can ask employers, schools, councils and NHS trusts whether their policies reflect the Supreme Court judgment and current EHRC guidance, rather than Stonewall-style ideology.

**Opening line:** "If the law says sex matters, why are women still being told to move aside?"

**Title:** *Single-sex spaces: watchdog challenges trans activist misinformation*

### 4. [Parents and pastors face prison as Scotland hears only one side](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxONXBYODcwLWY2V0FMX3kwbDBqUFd2YzV4QmlyRFoyb09yaFRyNjNWb3Aya3JWbHJMMzk1UGpPUko1QW5lNWsyR2tzM0tsNWFkZnpHYjZsVEdHaEs5MzRSR0d6bzN5WTU5QWVBSVJ4dWszeXZ6ME1jNWJUc1NfaVp1c3NlbDg1d1ZZVzZSSVZ1YUZtenNyYmRMTnhJZ1lSSXc?oc=5)
*Sexuality · Evangelical Times*

The report says Scotland is considering conversion practices legislation under which parents and pastors could face criminal penalties, while critics say the process has heard only one side. The concern is that ordinary Christian teaching, prayer and pastoral conversations could be treated as harmful conduct.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Matthew Grech was prosecuted in Malta for sharing his testimony of finding Christian faith and leaving a homosexual lifestyle; his case shows how conversion therapy laws can criminalise speech, testimony and pastoral care.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents talking to a child about sexuality or gender, pastors praying with someone who asks for help, and church youth workers giving biblical counsel. If the law is vague, people may self-censor long before anyone is prosecuted.

**Angle:** Our line is that abuse and coercion are already wrong, but vague conversion bans threaten consensual conversations and Christian discipleship. Viewers should understand the practical danger: the question is not whether cruelty should be banned, but whether prayer, repentance and biblical teaching become suspect.

**Opening line:** "Could a pastor be punished for praying with someone who asks for help?"

**Title:** *Scotland conversion therapy plans: could parents and pastors face prison?*

### 5. [Reform activist, 15, arrested after comparing Tory councillor to ‘rent boy’](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxPQm1sSXhPX0I2Z280eDhXdVNNOGVmTUtiM3h2Qkh6Z1V4WWU2MzNmeC1jYkdBMzhBczdmU0lrbUFqa1l4dlpqYmhySUplWng4elpSdWowTXBwTXZOZVFhbm54NEFOVDVBX3dNdFZ1eFR6YkpYOWtUclAzalp1NGphZUhDQ0pBS041MUp3N0dwR2VZOXBoRFRFSWt1bkFZYnNYUDJz?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · The Telegraph*

A 15-year-old Reform activist was reportedly arrested after comparing a Conservative councillor to a 'rent boy'. The comment was crude and offensive, but the police response raises serious questions about proportionality and the criminalisation of political speech.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Anthony Stevens was arrested in front of his family over a handful of tweets defending free speech; his case shows how quickly online political speech can bring police to the door.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents whose teenagers post foolish or provocative things online, and local activists who argue fiercely about politics. It also affects councillors and campaigners who need robust debate without turning every insult into a police matter.

**Angle:** Our line is that offensive speech should usually be answered by criticism, not arrest. Viewers gain a simple principle they can apply across politics: if the police are used for insults and bad taste, they will eventually be used against beliefs the state dislikes.

**Opening line:** "Should a stupid teenage insult really end with an arrest?"

**Title:** *Teen activist arrested: are police criminalising political insults?*

The Times warns that a proposed Conversion Practices Bill could create legal trouble by catching ordinary conversations, prayer, pastoral care and parental guidance, not just coercive abuse. The concern is that vague wording would leave Christians unsure what they are allowed to say about sexuality, identity and change.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Matthew Grech was prosecuted in Malta for sharing his Christian testimony of leaving a homosexual lifestyle; his case shows how conversion-practices laws can criminalise speech and testimony.

**Who this hits:** This affects pastors, youth leaders, Christian counsellors and parents who may be asked for help by someone struggling with sexuality or gender. If the law is vague, they may self-censor rather than risk a police complaint.

**Angle:** We should say clearly that abuse and coercion are already wrong, but banning prayerful, consensual conversation is a direct threat to Christian ministry. Viewers will understand why the wording matters, and why they should ask MPs whether prayer, repentance, testimony and pastoral care will be explicitly protected.

**Opening line:** "Could praying with someone soon be treated as conversion therapy?"

**Title:** *Conversion Practices Bill: Could Christian Prayer Become a Crime?*

*Gender · GB News*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses were told to 'broaden their mindset' after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; their case shows exactly why clear single-sex guidance matters.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, teachers, gym users, hospital patients and women using changing rooms, toilets or refuges. It also affects employers who may now be under pressure to ignore the law in order to satisfy activists.

**Angle:** Our line should be that the law must protect women’s privacy, dignity and safety, not be rewritten by misinformation campaigns. Viewers will learn that the Supreme Court judgment is not theoretical: it should change what hospitals, councils, schools and employers do now.

**Opening line:** "If the law is clear, why are women still being told to move over?"

**Title:** *Single-Sex Spaces: EHRC Accuses Activists of Misleading the Public*

*Islam · organiser.org*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** John Steele was arrested and prosecuted after asking about the Qur'an's teaching on domestic violence; this report shows why such questions are legitimate matters of public concern, not hate speech.

**Who this hits:** This affects Muslim women and girls who may be trapped under coercive religious teaching, as well as teachers, police officers and councillors afraid to ask direct questions. It also affects Christians and others who are often accused of bigotry for raising safeguarding concerns.

**Angle:** We should argue that violence against women must never be excused by religion, and that Britain must not develop blasphemy rules that silence scrutiny of sharia teaching. Viewers will understand the difference between attacking Muslims and protecting vulnerable women by asking hard, necessary questions.

**Opening line:** "When does fear of offence leave women unprotected?"

**Title:** *London Imam Report: Why Sharia and Domestic Violence Must Be Scrutinised*

### 4. [‘Sadness cannot be a reason to die’ - Dublin woman slams clinic over mum’s assisted suicide](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*End of life · Sunday World*

A Dublin woman has criticised an assisted suicide clinic after her mother’s death, saying that sadness should not be treated as a reason to die. The story puts a human face on the danger of expanding assisted suicide beyond the terminally ill and into despair, loneliness or depression.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Sudiksha Thirumalesh fought for the right to keep living and seek treatment when others judged her situation hopeless; her case shows the danger of systems that decide vulnerable lives are no longer worth protecting.

**Who this hits:** This affects elderly parents, disabled people and anyone going through grief, depression or fear of becoming a burden. Families could find that a loved one is offered death when what they need is care, treatment and hope.

**Angle:** Our line should be that assisted suicide changes medicine from suicide prevention to suicide provision. Viewers will understand why safeguards fail when sadness, pressure or loneliness are treated as medical reasons for death, and why they should press MPs to invest in palliative care instead.

**Opening line:** "What happens when sadness becomes a reason for doctors to help someone die?"

**Title:** *Assisted Suicide: ‘Sadness Cannot Be a Reason to Die’*

### 5. [Mental Health Champion warns new school curriculum could harm pupil wellbeing and seeks independent review](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Education · Belfast Telegraph*

Northern Ireland’s Mental Health Champion has warned that a new school curriculum could harm pupil wellbeing and has called for an independent review. The warning puts pressure on education authorities to show that children’s mental health, parental concerns and safeguarding have been properly considered.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Kristie Higgs was sacked after raising concerns about relationships and sex education on Facebook, and Izzy Montague challenged LGBT teaching to very young children; both cases show why parents must be heard before schools impose contested material.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents with children in school now, especially those worried about what their children are being taught on sex, relationships and identity. It also affects teachers who may be expected to deliver lessons they believe are harmful.

**Angle:** We should say that children are not experiments, and major curriculum changes need transparency, evidence and parental consent. Viewers will know to ask their school what is being taught, whether materials can be viewed in advance, and how parents can raise concerns without being branded extreme.

**Opening line:** "Would you know if your child’s curriculum was harming their wellbeing?"

**Title:** *School Curriculum Warning: Parents Must Not Be Shut Out*

*Christian freedoms · Barnsley Chronicle*

A Christian social worker is taking a religious discrimination case to the Court of Appeal after being blocked from work over biblical beliefs expressed online. The case asks whether Christians can be excluded from caring professions simply for holding orthodox views on marriage and sexuality.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Felix Ngole is our client: he was expelled from a social work course over Facebook posts on biblical marriage, won at the Court of Appeal, and then missed out on a job for the same views.

**Who this hits:** Christian students and professionals in social work, teaching, nursing and counselling need to know whether their private beliefs can be used to end their careers. It also affects parents and vulnerable people who should not be told that Christian carers are automatically unsafe.

**Angle:** Our line is that public-service professions must not become belief tests where orthodox Christianity is treated as a safeguarding risk. Viewers will understand why this case matters beyond one job: it could shape whether Christians can train, qualify and work without renouncing biblical convictions.

**Opening line:** "Can a Christian be barred from social work for believing the Bible?"

**Title:** *Christian social worker takes belief case to Court of Appeal*

*Gender · BBC*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses are our clients: they objected to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman, raising the same practical issue of single-sex spaces in the NHS.

**Who this hits:** Female nurses, healthcare assistants and patients are directly affected when hospitals ignore sex-based privacy in changing rooms, wards or intimate care. Christian staff also need to know whether raising a safeguarding or conscience concern will be treated as misconduct.

**Angle:** Our line is that compassion for gender-confused people cannot mean removing privacy and dignity from women. Viewers will understand how the Supreme Court judgment on sex should matter in real workplaces, and why they should ask their NHS trust, employer or union what single-sex protections are actually in place.

**Opening line:** "Would your daughter’s nurse have a female-only changing room at work?"

**Title:** *Sandie Peggie tribunal tests single-sex rights in the NHS*

**Angle:** Our line is that Prevent was created to stop terrorism, not to police Christian sermons in schools. Viewers will understand why parents should ask schools what pupils are being taught about LGBT and gender issues, and how staff who dissent are being treated.

**Who this hits:** This affects police officers who may feel unable to question one-sided training, and members of the public who expect the police to protect free speech rather than police approved opinions. Christians in public service will ask whether they can speak honestly about Islam or immigration without being branded hateful.

**Angle:** Our line should be that police training must distinguish hatred against Muslims from legitimate criticism of Islam, politics or public policy. Aleteia reports that a Dutch cardinal has condemned the euthanasia of a toddler, rejecting the claim that ending the child’s life was merciful. The story is a stark example from a country where euthanasia has already gone far beyond the terminally ill adult cases often used to sell the policy.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Indi Gregory’s parents fought court orders to remove life support despite an offer of treatment in Italy; while this Dutch case is active euthanasia, both expose how vulnerable children can be treated as lives no longer worth fighting for.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents of seriously ill children and families caring for disabled or medically fragile relatives. It also matters to anyone watching assisted suicide debates in the UK and wondering where the line will really be drawn.

**Angle:** We should explain that once killing is renamed compassion, the pressure falls hardest on those who cannot speak for themselves. Viewers will see why Christians insist on palliative care, protection for the vulnerable and a refusal to measure a child’s worth by health or disability.

*Gender · Belfast Telegraph*

A tribunal has heard that nurse Sandie Peggie was suspended because of her conduct, not her beliefs, after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male who identifies as a woman. The case goes to the heart of how NHS employers treat women who raise single-sex safeguarding concerns.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses were told to 'broaden their mindset' after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; Sandie Peggie's case raises the same single-sex workplace issue.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, doctors and other staff who use changing rooms, toilets or wards at work and are unsure whether they can object without risking discipline. It also affects female patients who expect intimate care and private spaces to recognise biological sex.

**Angle:** Our line is that calling this 'conduct' must not become a way to punish women for stating biological reality. Viewers will see why the Supreme Court judgment on sex matters in ordinary workplaces, not just in courtrooms. They can ask their employer whether policies protect lawful single-sex spaces and whether staff may raise concerns without retaliation.

**Opening line:** "Can a nurse be punished for objecting to a man in the changing room?"

**Title:** *Sandie Peggie Tribunal: Are Women Allowed to Defend Single-Sex Spaces?*

### 3. [Northern Ireland MLAs back 'conversion therapy' bill despite concerns over prayer and parenting](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Sexuality · Belfast News Letter*

Northern Ireland MLAs have backed a proposed 'conversion therapy' bill despite concerns that it could catch prayer, pastoral conversations and parents guiding their children. The story is a live warning about how broad conversion practices bans can reach far beyond coercion or abuse.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Matthew Grech was prosecuted in Malta for sharing his testimony of finding faith and leaving a homosexual lifestyle; this is the kind of speech and prayer that broad conversion therapy laws can criminalise.

**Who this hits:** This affects pastors, youth leaders, Christian parents and anyone who might pray with a person who wants to live according to biblical teaching on sexuality. It also affects teenagers and adults who actively want Christian support but may find churches frightened into silence.

**Angle:** We should make clear that coercion and abuse are already wrong, but consensual prayer and pastoral care must not be treated as crimes. Viewers will understand the difference between banning abuse and banning Christian discipleship. They can contact representatives and ask for explicit protections for prayer, preaching, parenting and voluntary conversations.

**Opening line:** "Could praying with someone become a criminal offence in Northern Ireland?"

**Title:** *Northern Ireland Conversion Therapy Bill: Prayer and Parenting at Risk?*

### 4. [Taxpayer-funded police training likened Nigel Farage and GB News to Islamophobia](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxPa2tpTHo0ZmtvdVBDWEpPcVJhTkQ3RzFBRVFzY0ZDbGtkRTRDV0pPT3ZCWmpXRDBXbTZlSEI2eXNuMWtzQU1pS3EwUE80UTc5LVpKazZlSnJZRlcwQXlIREJ0TG9jd21aR09pa2ptb1Q0S2xERTktLTY3Sy1OczF6UjJQZHpObi15SXpOeDRacmFleWV0cW5DOA?oc=5)
*Islam · GB News*

A report says taxpayer-funded police training materials linked Nigel Farage and GB News with Islamophobia. The concern is that police and public bodies are being trained to treat mainstream political or religious criticism of Islam as a form of hostility.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Luke Salmons was suspended and forced to resign as a police community support officer after questioning Islam during mandatory diversity training; this story shows the same danger inside policing culture.

**Who this hits:** This affects police officers, council staff, teachers and public-sector workers who may be told in training that ordinary criticism of Islam is misconduct. It also affects Christians who evangelise or discuss Islamic teaching in public and need police to protect lawful speech, not police it.

**Angle:** Our line is that genuine anti-Muslim hatred must be opposed, but criticism of Islam, politicians or media outlets is not the same thing. Viewers will understand how vague 'Islamophobia' training can chill lawful speech before anyone is arrested. They can ask local police and councils what definitions they use and whether training protects freedom of religion and expression.

**Opening line:** "Are police being trained to treat criticism of Islam as hate?"

**Title:** *Taxpayer-Funded Police Training and the New Blasphemy Code*

*Freedom of speech · GB News*

A Labour MP has compared Epping migrant hotel protesters to Palestine Action, a proscribed terror group. Whatever one thinks of the protest, the story raises the serious issue of politicians using terrorism language about lawful public dissent.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bernard Randall was reported to Prevent, the government's terrorism watchdog, over a school sermon on identity politics; his case shows how extremism language can be stretched to target lawful belief and speech.

**Who this hits:** This affects local residents who want to protest controversial decisions without being branded extremists or terror-adjacent. It also affects Christians and others who speak publicly on unpopular issues and fear that one inflammatory label could bring police, employers or safeguarding officers to their door.

**Angle:** We should not defend abuse or disorder, but we should insist that terror labels are not political insults. Viewers will understand why loose extremism language eventually threatens ordinary people, including Christians. They can ask MPs and local police to distinguish clearly between criminal behaviour and peaceful protest.

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Christian 'discriminated' against in job retraction over LGBT views, court hears](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiXkFVX3lxTE43VUNtR21VTHJoaExWSURhb0pPM1FWb0loazJtRDc0cGlYLTZzSlFVdC1NNGxrZTVVSFVvNU5KUHJhSmhkOHNpdFVUX0Y4LVlSTmtzdGtaa0ZvRklBTVE?oc=5)
*Christian Concern in the news · BBC*

The BBC reports that a court has heard a Christian was discriminated against when a job offer was withdrawn over his views on LGBT issues. The case concerns whether an employer can treat orthodox Christian beliefs on marriage and sexuality as a professional risk.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** This is our client Felix Ngole: he was expelled from a social work course over biblical marriage posts, won at the Court of Appeal, and then missed out on a job for the same beliefs.

**Who this hits:** This affects Christians applying for jobs in social work, counselling, education, healthcare or charities who are asked whether their beliefs make them unsafe. It also affects anyone whose old social media posts could be used to block them from work.

**Angle:** Our line is simple: Christians must not be treated as unemployable because they hold biblical beliefs about marriage and sexuality. Viewers will understand why Felix’s case matters beyond one job offer — and why they should not assume an employer is allowed to punish lawful Christian belief.

**Opening line:** "Can a Christian be blocked from a job for believing in biblical marriage?"

**Title:** *Christian job offer withdrawn over LGBT beliefs: Felix Ngole in court*

### 2. [Trans row nurse tells Sandie Peggie employment tribunal that union 'failed to help me when I needed them most'](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Gender · Sky News*

Sky News reports that nurse Sandie Peggie told her employment tribunal her union failed to help her when she objected to sharing a changing room with a biological male who identifies as a woman. The case is being watched closely after the Supreme Court clarified the meaning of sex in equality law.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses faced the same issue: they objected to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman and were told to 'broaden their mindset'.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, carers and other women at work who need private changing spaces and do not know whether management or unions will back them. It also affects patients who expect sex-based privacy and dignity in healthcare.

**Angle:** We should say this is not a fringe dispute about language, but a practical question: can women say no to undressing beside a man at work? Viewers will understand what the Supreme Court judgment should mean on the ground, and why employees should ask their workplace and union what policy they are actually applying.

**Opening line:** "What happens when a nurse says no to sharing a changing room with a man?"

**Title:** *Sandie Peggie tribunal: are women’s changing rooms still single-sex?*

### 3. [Victory! Northern Ireland Conversion Practices Ban Bill passes key vote](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipgFBVV95cUxOeDlFQlJsNTZKRlRpNUlBSGlueDJ1d1VnM1FYRlppQmtyVXEwa21KdDZsN2R3andSQ3htTFlpNHdYSW5TLUhTX1dCb2FmWFJKZ3ZPRC1yTEtPQU5PRHRJdFZHQlducVZrNC14ci1JZ00tSDZ4aGlEaVh2N2hWWTFrejBuRFlRdllDZjFoMDFEUGdwSFAxV0lsaGpvRVZ6WWd3MThSTmJB?oc=5)
*Sexuality · Humanists UK*

Humanists UK is celebrating after a proposed Conversion Practices Ban Bill in Northern Ireland passed a key vote. The Bill is not law yet, but it has moved forward and could affect prayer, pastoral care, counselling and personal testimony if drafted broadly.

*Christian Concern in the news · Daily Express*

The Daily Express reports that nurses are due to give evidence against a union they say abandoned them during a dispute over a trans-identifying biological male using their changing room. The case puts workplace single-sex spaces, union representation and the practical meaning of sex in law directly in the spotlight.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Darlington Nurses: we represent nurses who were told to 'broaden their mindset' after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, care workers and other women who are expected to change clothes or be vulnerable at work. It also affects union members who assume their union will defend them when they raise a lawful safeguarding concern.

**Angle:** Our line is that women should not have to choose between their dignity, their job and their union membership. Viewers will understand why the Supreme Court judgment on sex matters in ordinary workplaces, and what questions to ask if their employer or union still treats self-identification as overriding biological sex.

**Opening line:** "Would your union defend you for asking for a female-only changing room?"

**Title:** *Nurses take on union after trans changing-room row*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Indi Gregory and Sudiksha Thirumalesh both fought hospital and court decisions over life-sustaining treatment; their cases show why vulnerable patients and families need better care and protection, not a system that moves more quickly towards death.

**Who this hits:** This affects anyone caring for an elderly parent, a disabled relative or a seriously ill child. It is about whether your loved one receives time, pain relief, advocacy and hope — or feels like a burden in a broken system.

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Peggie’s beliefs had ‘no bearing’ on union decision to refuse support – tribunal](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxOWXBkX1M0YW9TcEJyTVZSSkhGOTZHUVduUHNRdDBjZ0VhNk1ibHNBV1hjRUg0dEw2aTRTUnl2bjFVLXAxaVRkN0xsWTVQV3NXUWRkeGRkY1FUR3UybHRhN0VvTWExQmlaY0tXY1B6V0RLVGtiLUlGQnFMSGhFR1F0ZmNQT3RLTmRwcW43UGE0aS1yS0dLaHM5VTNXVktGMDhDWm5zUm41b0VEbjFKblg1bDF3MzlFUQ?oc=5)
*Gender · Edp24*

A tribunal has ruled that Sandie Peggie’s beliefs had no bearing on a union decision not to support her after she objected to sharing a changing room with a male colleague who identifies as a woman. The case keeps the spotlight on whether women in the NHS can raise privacy and safety concerns without being left isolated.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** We represent the Darlington Nurses, who were told to ‘broaden their mindset’ after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, midwives and care staff who may be expected to use changing rooms or intimate facilities with male colleagues. It also affects union members who assume their union will defend them if they raise a safeguarding or dignity concern.

**Angle:** Our line is that women should not have to choose between their job, their union support and their basic privacy. Viewers will understand why the Supreme Court judgment on sex matters in ordinary workplaces, and why staff should put concerns in writing and ask employers how policies comply with the law.

**Opening line:** "What happens when a nurse asks for a female-only changing room?"

**Title:** *Nurse left exposed after raising female-only changing room concerns*

### 2. [Campaigner for domestic abuse survivors hounded by trans activists](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiowFBVV95cUxOQ1VqckNnbEt6WE1YMmtvTHlKZUNIcHRBUFplaTVuMkhONWZaLWxEV05QY1dUNklrQmd1SHp3QzdTWk9abmtYZnFJZ2ZSWnE4VkZ6eDVlbTMxZXpjcUtUZ2JqRHZpR2JOZ3lPUVJkUFU1VnJTNnNnUFJfWnNpd09saVkyME9Pd29EZXFoNDBZNnVhNHBmOWNESUFwaV92ak9zLV9N?oc=5)
*Gender · The Christian Institute*

The Christian Institute reports that a campaigner for domestic abuse survivors has been targeted by trans activists after speaking up for women’s safety and single-sex provision. The story shows how even work protecting traumatised women can become controversial when biological sex is denied.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** We represent the Darlington Nurses, whose concerns about a biological male in a women’s changing room raise the same issue: women are being punished for saying privacy and safety matter.

**Who this hits:** This affects women fleeing male violence, refuge workers, counsellors and volunteers who need clear single-sex boundaries. It also affects any woman afraid to speak up because she might be branded hateful for asking for female-only support.

**Angle:** Our line is that safeguarding women is not bigotry. Viewers will see how gender ideology moves from abstract language into real services for vulnerable women, and why churches and charities should ask whether their policies still protect single-sex care.

**Opening line:** "Can a women’s refuge still say it is for women?"

**Title:** *Domestic abuse campaigner targeted for defending women-only spaces*

### 3. [Judgment in our case about guidance on sexual consent](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilwFBVV95cUxPSW1BWVJGNE1iSG1tN3FaNTVNT0VRcHJiS0FFM3hhSFdQSGdmZGJEUUJuTDkxX2JOdnV4WDY2c28yLU5qaWhLTlBjMXlXSWhaUnBQbzdVcHpNNTJaOHV4WThucExHRFBLRWZZMDJ3bnJGSzh0b0w0a21rMUVVMzZOczlqQWttTFdPbS1rdTZCdHhzSFZXamtn?oc=5)
*Gender · Sex Matters*

Sex Matters has reported a judgment in its legal challenge concerning guidance on sexual consent and the relevance of biological sex. The case raises the basic question of whether truth about sex matters when a person is deciding whether to consent to intimacy.

**Who this hits:** This affects young adults, parents of teenagers, students and anyone trying to understand what consent means in a culture of gender self-identification. It also affects police, prosecutors and educators who give guidance on sex and relationships.

**Angle:** Our line is that consent must be based on reality, not on compelled belief in someone’s gender identity. Viewers will understand why ‘sex is real’ is not a culture-war slogan but a safeguard for dignity, honesty and personal boundaries.

**Opening line:** "Does consent mean anything if biological sex can be hidden?"

**Title:** *Sex, truth and consent: why this judgment matters*

### 4. [Chair of Jersey assisted suicide service wrote that it harms people](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiogFBVV95cUxOb0JjQjJXdXFZTExYNy0tVTZmakdudk9RZE5VR0RndGpVUkkyZ2pBWnppQVRiQ1FrY0UzZi1Bc1RxbnJzUGNRaUYySkhzZ1hWcU16UDhQRXh2bHItOG4yazVLdkEtTkJkb3NGcXZsZHJkbk82T0dyeUFBcnl5Y1BPbHQ0cjY1N1IzTFU0dk9IdUpPMzl4ekYxMTRCZU9VWmpzN0E?oc=5)
*End of life · Christian Action Research and Education*

CARE reports that the chair of Jersey’s assisted suicide service previously wrote that assisted suicide harms people. The report comes as Jersey moves further down the road towards making assisted suicide part of healthcare.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** We represented families such as Indi Gregory’s and Sudiksha Thirumalesh’s, who fought medical systems that decided death was in a patient’s best interests rather than backing every possible chance of life.

**Who this hits:** This affects elderly, disabled and seriously ill people, first in Jersey and then across the UK as politicians watch what happens there. It also affects families who worry that a sick relative may be offered death before being offered better care, pain relief or practical support.

**Angle:** Our line is that assisted suicide is not a harmless private choice once the state and doctors build a service around it. Viewers will understand why safeguards often fail the vulnerable, and why they should ask MPs whether palliative care is being properly funded before assisted suicide is even considered.

**Opening line:** "What if the person leading assisted suicide has already said it harms people?"

**Title:** *Jersey assisted suicide chair’s warning exposes the danger*

### 5. [Edinburgh University axes Divinity degrees](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipwFBVV95cUxPNDZUa29VeFY0TVJmQlRFdDE3TVYwYVJJdFhEZ1BoaHV6Q1hURVRLZklodjRKSnphYUtxLVE1SlBjRXc3c0FKak1rRjdwNm9EUUc0MHNYaWZKVVhlcXp2dTJPVHZBVmRDR0w5Q2w3T3c4TlhJOUxuTURnQWo4T1NYNF8wS3Z1a0pSVUdxNm5XZG9DN293c2VXWWVqSkt3Q2QxOTJOV0xjQQ?oc=5)
*Christian society · Premier Christian News*

Premier Christian News reports that the University of Edinburgh is axing Divinity degrees. The decision is a concrete example of historic Christian learning being pushed out of major public institutions.

**Who this hits:** This affects prospective students who want serious theological education at a historic university, and churches that need well-trained pastors, teachers and thinkers. It also affects parents and grandparents who wonder why Britain’s Christian heritage is disappearing from places that once shaped it.

**Angle:** Our line is that this is not just one university course being cut; it is part of a wider loss of Christian memory in national life. Viewers will understand why Christian education matters beyond the church, and can ask universities, donors and church leaders what they are doing to protect it.

**Opening line:** "Why is one of Britain’s great universities cutting Divinity?"

**Title:** *Edinburgh axes Divinity degrees as Christian memory fades*

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Sandie Peggie says union did not take her case seriously](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiXkFVX3lxTFA2X3c2RWhLYTFEb0d5TkdiSmtPYTBvQ2Q1c09wM0tYcnFYZ09oSG1EYjI4a0ZRMnl5MzFiXzFvU2sxWkRUdnhPNFJ4XzZFaEtEZDJheFA2NW1Zb2JJUnc?oc=5)
*Gender · bbc.co.uk*

Nurse Sandie Peggie says her union failed to take her seriously after she objected to sharing a changing room with a biologically male doctor who identifies as a woman. The case has become a test of whether NHS staff can rely on unions and employers to protect single-sex spaces after the Supreme Court judgment on sex.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses faced the same issue: nurses objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male and being told to change their attitude rather than being protected.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, carers and NHS staff who are told to use changing rooms or intimate facilities with members of the opposite sex. It also matters for patients who expect privacy, dignity and same-sex care in hospitals.

**Angle:** Our line is that women should not have to fight their employer and their union simply to keep a female changing room female. Viewers will understand that the Supreme Court judgment is not self-enforcing: staff need to ask whether their hospital, union or regulator has actually changed policy in line with the law.

**Opening line:** "If your union won’t defend your changing room, who will?"

**Title:** *Sandie Peggie and the Fight for Single-Sex NHS Spaces*

### 2. [Tell Northern Ireland Assembly not to criminalise conversion practices](https://christianconcern.com/action/tell-northern-ireland-assembly-not-to-criminalise-conversion-practices/)
*Sexuality · Christian Concern*

The Northern Ireland Assembly is consulting on a Conversion Practices Criminalisation Bill. Christian Concern warns that, as drafted, it could criminalise consensual prayer, pastoral conversation and Christian teaching about sexuality and identity.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Matthew Grech was prosecuted in Malta for sharing his Christian testimony of leaving a homosexual lifestyle, showing how conversion-practices laws can punish ordinary testimony and pastoral speech.

**Who this hits:** This affects pastors, youth leaders, Christian parents and anyone asked by a friend or family member for prayer about sexuality or gender. If the law is badly drafted, conversations that are voluntary and compassionate could still become legally risky.

**Angle:** Our line is that abuse and coercion should already be unlawful, but prayer and consensual Christian counsel must not be treated as a crime. Viewers get something practical: they can respond to the consultation and ask MLAs to protect ordinary pastoral care before the wording becomes law.

**Opening line:** "Could praying with someone become a criminal offence in Northern Ireland?"

**Title:** *Northern Ireland’s Conversion Bill: Why Christians Must Respond*

### 3. [Ex TVP-chief says there is "absolutely" still grooming gangs in Oxford](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxONHZWUHV5SGdFZGRjb0Qta1gxcEY0UGZVVGs1ZFpLQms0eUJzQm1JTVJGQlJlQVJZeE9TU0VOZDRZb2IzNllaSmNpMEFBUlM2X2ZEQWloYVVUS0p5SDBkdGdyUkEyOFQwMzhTV0owcmZRUkFITnFjWi1SMkxWWFQ1eDNBUUExNTBhMkhLQjhXbmZudHZnVlA1YWJjYw?oc=5)
*Islam · Oxford Mail*

A former Thames Valley Police chief has said there are still grooming gangs operating in Oxford. The comments come in the shadow of Operation Bullfinch and continuing questions about whether police, councils and social services have learned the lessons of past abuse.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** 'Sarah' was subjected to exactly this kind of abuse: groomed as a child, repeatedly raped, forced into sharia marriages, forcibly converted to Islam and failed by authorities who should have protected her.

**Who this hits:** This affects teenage girls, parents and communities who have been told for years that the problem is historic or solved. It also affects survivors who need authorities to speak honestly about religious, cultural and institutional failures.

**Angle:** Our line is that protecting children must come before protecting reputations or avoiding difficult conversations about Islam, sharia and grooming gangs. Viewers will understand why vague safeguarding language is not enough: they can ask local councillors and police whether current gangs, forced conversion and religious coercion are being openly investigated.

**Opening line:** "What if grooming gangs in Oxford are not just history?"

**Title:** *Oxford Grooming Gangs: Former Police Chief Says They Still Exist*

### 4. [Evangelist acquitted of a public order offence after he was prosecuted for giving out gospel literature in Soho](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Christian freedoms · Evangelical Times*

An evangelist has been acquitted after being prosecuted for a public order offence for giving out gospel literature in Soho. The case raises fresh concerns about police and prosecutors treating peaceful Christian witness as public disorder.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bread of Life Community Church faced a Community Protection Notice seeking to control the content of its street evangelism, showing the same pattern of public-order powers being used against gospel preaching.

**Who this hits:** This affects street preachers, church outreach teams and ordinary Christians handing out leaflets in town centres. It also affects anyone who assumes public evangelism is lawful, only to find police or councils treating it as a nuisance.

**Angle:** Our line is that giving out the gospel in public is not a crime, even when some people dislike the message. Viewers will understand that acquittals matter because the process itself can punish Christians through arrest, stress and legal costs, and they should know to seek advice if police try to stop lawful witness.

**Opening line:** "Since when is handing out gospel leaflets a public order offence?"

**Title:** *Evangelist Acquitted After Gospel Leaflet Prosecution*

### 5. [Assisted-Suicide Bill Defeated in U.K. as Lawmakers Raise Concerns Over Vulnerable People](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*End of life · Crosswalk.com*

Lawmakers have defeated an assisted-suicide bill after concerns were raised about risks to vulnerable people. The vote is a significant setback for campaigners who want doctors to be able to help patients end their lives.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Indi Gregory, Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Rashid Abbasi were not assisted-suicide cases, but they show why end-of-life law matters: families and patients can already be overruled when institutions decide treatment should stop.

**Who this hits:** This affects elderly, disabled, seriously ill and depressed people who may fear becoming a burden. It also affects families who want reassurance that doctors will offer care, pain relief and hope rather than a route to death.

**Angle:** Our line is that this defeat is welcome because safeguards cannot remove the pressure vulnerable people may feel once assisted suicide is normalised. Viewers will understand that the debate is not over, and that the practical alternative Christians should press for is better palliative care, protection for conscience and a refusal to treat suffering people as disposable.

**Opening line:** "Would assisted suicide make vulnerable people feel safer, or more expendable?"

**Title:** *Assisted-Suicide Bill Defeated: Why the Vulnerable Still Need Protection*

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Trans row nurse Sandie Peggie at centre of second employment tribunal against nursing union](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Gender · Daily Record*

Nurse Sandie Peggie is reportedly at the centre of a second employment tribunal, this time involving her nursing union, after the row over a trans-identifying doctor and women’s changing spaces.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Darlington Nurses were told to ‘broaden their mindset’ after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman; Jennifer Melle’s case also involves NHS staff, pronouns and compelled speech.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses, midwives and healthcare assistants who may be told to accept mixed-sex changing spaces or risk being treated as the problem. It also affects female patients who expect dignity, privacy and safety in NHS settings.

**Angle:** Our line is that women should not have to lose their privacy, their jobs or union support for stating the reality of biological sex. Viewers will understand why the Supreme Court judgment on sex matters in ordinary workplaces, and why they should ask whether their NHS trust or employer is actually following the law.

**Opening line:** "Can a nurse lose union support for objecting to a man in women’s changing rooms?"

**Title:** *Nurse tribunal exposes the cost of defending single-sex spaces*

### 2. [Mother sounds alarm as controversial end-of-life Professor to take charge of ‘palliating’ her brain-injured son after withdrawal of food and fluids](https://christianconcern.com/ccpressreleases/mother-sounds-alarm-as-controversial-end-of-life-professor-to-take-charge-of-palliating-her-brain-injured-son-after-withdrawal-of-food-and-fluids/)
*End of life · Christian Legal Centre*

Christian Legal Centre reports that a mother is raising urgent concerns after a controversial end-of-life professor is set to oversee the ‘palliating’ of her brain-injured son following the withdrawal of food and fluids. The story sits alongside a forthcoming Supreme Court case concerning the death of Robert Barnor at St Helier Hospital.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Rashid Abbasi, Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Indi Gregory all involved families being overruled by hospitals or courts in life-and-death treatment decisions.

**Who this hits:** This affects families sitting beside a seriously ill child, parent or spouse and being told that doctors, not the family, will decide when treatment, food or fluids stop. It is especially concrete for anyone with a loved one in intensive care or long-term hospital care.

**Angle:** Our line is that vulnerable patients must not be written off, and families must not be treated as obstacles when they are fighting for life. Viewers will understand what ‘best interests’ decisions can mean in practice: not an abstract legal phrase, but food, fluids and treatment being withdrawn from someone who cannot speak for themselves.

**Opening line:** "What happens when doctors decide your loved one’s life should end?"

**Title:** *Mother warns over hospital end-of-life decision for brain-injured son*

### 3. [Christian grandmother, 83, 'euthanised against her will' under assisted dying system in Canada](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilgFBVV95cUxPaGtnUUZ6X3l6ZEwxYkw2UXlkeE5ucTBKM3RNNmROcXUxOURFRk01TE5WQllXSldEWklvS2dEYks4Zlh3Y0wxdUduME9MV2QzelhYaEhsTXl2MkQzUG1lalQwMjc1dWFVa0lXMG1IZ2dSUVlmaTRGN19Ob0dvYXZLOXFTYXRiUDZnZGVwTkpsRFhPYzNlTXc?oc=5)
*End of life · gbnews.com*

GB News reports that an 83-year-old Christian grandmother in Canada was allegedly euthanised against her will under Canada’s assisted dying system. The case is being presented as a warning about what can happen once assisted suicide becomes normalised.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Our end-of-life cases, including Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Indi Gregory, did not involve assisted suicide, but they show the same danger: vulnerable people and families being overruled when life-ending medical decisions are made.

**Who this hits:** This affects elderly parents and grandparents, disabled people and anyone who fears becoming a ‘burden’ in a healthcare system under pressure. It also affects families who are told that legal safeguards will protect their loved ones, but want to know what happens when those safeguards fail.

**Angle:** Our line is that assisted suicide does not remain a private choice for long; it changes the way doctors, families and institutions view frail human life. Viewers will gain a concrete example to raise with MPs and friends when told that assisted dying laws are always tightly controlled and safe.

**Opening line:** "Canada was promised safeguards. Why is a grandmother now said to be dead against her will?"

**Title:** *Canadian euthanasia case is a warning for the UK*

### 4. [Christians Came Together to Help Defeat UK’s Assisted Dying Bill](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxOR0h0Q1kyaGloV0pNSkloM0JHMEwzb1RuazhrZ2xZUGUxSEU3NlBMOGFDUlJsdld3ZXJrS3BMazJ4Y2gyYTV4Nlk4SmdQWF9obmdOeHpVcEtEbWxNcmFaY0RGcmFmZUYzQ3RGZzFaSEUtc0ZzNDBPNlFzZzhWNDUtM1pCZ09vM1ZuWEF3aGRtTjhoaHQ3dDViUDl5OA?oc=5)
*End of life · christianitytoday.com*

Christianity Today reports that Christians across the UK helped defeat an Assisted Dying Bill. The story presents the result as a significant moment of Christian mobilisation against legalising assisted suicide.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Rashid Abbasi, Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Indi Gregory show why end-of-life law is not theoretical: families can find themselves fighting hospitals and courts for the life of someone they love.

**Who this hits:** This affects disabled people, elderly relatives, people with terminal diagnoses and families worried about pressure to choose death rather than care. It also affects churchgoers who want to know whether writing, praying and speaking to MPs actually makes a difference.

**Angle:** Our line is that this is a moment to thank God, thank MPs who stood firm, and prepare for the issue to return. Viewers will see that ordinary Christians can shape public life, and that the next step is to keep pressing for better palliative care rather than assisted suicide.

**Opening line:** "Did Christian voices just help stop assisted suicide becoming law?"

**Title:** *How Christians helped defeat the Assisted Dying Bill*

### 5. [Pornhub investigated over its age checks](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6eq8dw3dlyqo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)
*Sexuality · BBC News (UK)*

The BBC reports that the regulator is investigating Pornhub over concerns about its age-check systems, including reliance on third-party checks provided by Apple for some users. The issue is whether children are still able to access explicit material despite new online safety requirements.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents giving a child a first smartphone, grandparents worried about what children see online, and teenagers being exposed to violent or degrading pornography. It is not a distant policy row: it is about what can appear on a child’s screen tonight.

**Angle:** Our line is that children need real protection, not box-ticking by porn companies or tech platforms. Viewers will understand why age checks matter but also why parents should not outsource safeguarding to regulators: they can ask what filters are on devices, speak to schools, and have honest conversations at home.

**Opening line:** "Can Pornhub still be reached by children despite age-check laws?"

**Title:** *Pornhub age-check investigation: what parents need to know*

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Health Minister tells nurses: "No plan for new rules"](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijgFBVV95cUxPWEtVQjBad2hxanFPTXRjblJlZUJOSnpncXJoV21sdk1JbnhDTUlqUEItRFAtQ1JaSUxoMVo2Y0xLMVA3NEpOQlNWb2xRZnpicEloTktFZFFpbTFSX29UOFozQl94djRLQS05bUhucHpPakpwb3ZUSkQyRW9CaF9rU19lQ1RUSVdUbWRWRXJ3?oc=5)
*Christian Concern in the news · Christian Concern*

Christian Concern reports that a Health Minister has told nurses there is “no plan for new rules” after concerns about single-sex changing facilities and NHS compliance with the law on biological sex. The story follows continuing questions after the Supreme Court judgment on the meaning of sex.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses were told to “broaden their mindset” after objecting to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman.

**Who this hits:** This affects nurses changing before and after a shift, women patients on wards, and any NHS worker who wants to know whether single-sex spaces will actually be protected. The practical issue is simple: who can use which changing room, ward or intimate-care space tomorrow?

**Angle:** Our line is that ministerial reassurance is not enough if NHS trusts are left to keep policies that ignore biological sex. Viewers will understand that the Supreme Court judgment matters in real workplaces, and that they can ask their MP or local NHS trust what written policy now protects women’s spaces.

**Opening line:** "A minister says no new rules—but what protects nurses changing for work tomorrow?"

**Title:** *Health minister response leaves nurses asking: who protects single-sex changing rooms?*

### 2. [Grooming victims see their abusers on the streets of Oxford](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxNRDQxdm40VnJhY0c5YTVROWZNTV80RlhMVHRscmlxMkVwMldfX1ZGOUltakhaR0VILU5UQzRoZlljLXEtRkJ5X3lMSU5lNTQyQ0g5VTh3WHI5dFlHejcwSWl3SGhNZEdNdG9Qb3YwR0FzQ0Z5bFQ0WFRscHhic1RickluWG9ZMmlOZGhtcjlBWlpwSThMSTdiSg?oc=5)
*Islam · The Times*

The Times reports that victims of the Oxford grooming gangs have seen men who abused them back on local streets. The story shows that for survivors, the scandal is not a closed chapter but a daily reality.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** ‘Sarah’ was groomed, raped, forced into sharia marriages, forcibly converted to Islam and subjected to forced abortions; her case shows the same pattern of abuse, intimidation and institutional failure.

**Who this hits:** This affects survivors who still live near the men who destroyed their childhoods, and parents who want to know whether police and councils will act when girls are at risk. It also affects communities where fear of being called racist or Islamophobic has silenced warnings.

**Angle:** Our line is that grooming gangs must not be treated as yesterday’s scandal while victims are still facing their abusers today. Viewers will understand why inquiries, policing and social services must confront every factor involved, including religion and culture, without hiding behind accusations of prejudice.

**Opening line:** "What if your abuser was back on your street?"

**Title:** *Oxford grooming victims still face their abusers: why this scandal is not over*

### 3. [Assisted dying BLOCKED from becoming law after MPs vote against historic bill](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifEFVX3lxTE1YSEJuS2pLRjgtZWRIeFlqOG1UMUtjbUxEblNrZW5fdFRadmpONjB2ZUZ0ZGN0VHdnMXI5NDdEOGswUkliVklRZ0duMFdUc1hjQmVtOFdNMDRqYXRyZGZtaktNQ25najRuZG9MQjVIUm91SFhwNl9CNC1qWkI?oc=5)
*End of life · GB News*

MPs have voted against an assisted dying bill, blocking it from becoming law through this route. It is a major moment in the national debate over whether doctors should be allowed to help patients end their lives.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Rashid Abbasi, Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Indi Gregory show the same end-of-life danger from another angle: vulnerable patients and families can be overruled when life is treated as negotiable.

**Who this hits:** This affects elderly, disabled, seriously ill and depressed people who could one day be offered death instead of care. It also affects families who worry that a sick relative may feel they are a burden.

**Angle:** Our line is that this vote is a reprieve, not the end of the battle. Viewers will understand why assisted suicide is not just about “choice”, but about pressure, prognosis, underfunded care and what kind of medicine we want for our parents and grandparents.

**Opening line:** "Assisted suicide has been stopped—for now. Will Parliament try again?"

**Title:** *Assisted dying bill defeated: a reprieve for vulnerable patients*

### 1. ['Hundreds' of Asian grooming gang members roaming free in Oxford with women spotting men who abused them after they avoided justice](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Islam · Daily Mail*

The Daily Mail reports that survivors in Oxford say hundreds of Asian grooming gang members who avoided justice are still free, with some women recognising men who abused them in the street. The story points to alleged failures by police and local authorities to secure justice for victims.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** 'Sarah' was groomed at 15 and subjected to repeated rape, forced sharia marriages, forced conversion to Islam and forced abortions; her case shows why victims must not be silenced when they describe exactly what happened to them.

**Who this hits:** This affects survivors who may still be living near their abusers, and parents who want to know whether authorities are telling the truth about risks to girls. It also affects social workers, police and councillors who must choose between institutional reputation and protecting children.

**Angle:** We should say plainly that this is not ancient history for the women who still see their abusers walking free. Viewers will understand why euphemisms and fear of being called racist or Islamophobic can protect perpetrators, and why they should press MPs, councils and police forces for transparent inquiries, prosecutions and victim support.

**Opening line:** "What if the men who abused you were still walking past you in Oxford?"

**Title:** *Oxford Grooming Gangs: Why Victims Are Still Being Failed*

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** The Darlington Nurses objected to sharing a changing room with a biological male identifying as a woman, and were told to 'broaden their mindset'; this is the same practical question in another single-sex space.

**Who this hits:** This affects women and girls using toilets in schools, hospitals, workplaces, shops and public buildings. It also affects managers who are writing policies now and need to know whether women can expect female-only facilities.

**Angle:** Our line is that biological sex is real, and privacy and dignity cannot be protected if any male can enter female facilities by self-identification. Viewers will learn the practical question to ask their school, employer or council: after the Supreme Court ruling, who is allowed into women-only spaces, and how will women’s objections be handled?

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [Senedd rejects calls for a Wales-specific grooming gangs inquiry](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilgFBVV95cUxQcENYLTI5NmlRZ0dkSzNoSmpkWXdwaW1tcnN5dEt2eXBja1BnWlJ3RDFhalNFOXZLSUFiZWx3UUhoMW4xTGdSVWJ4OVJ1M0ZGb1dBYnFXVE95QzBsQUNidHpUSnFoZllYcVdjRUVXMDdNemp4MFBuNHdGUDJNRndWeWFOTUJDTW5tUGdVXzExMVU5MTRVdHc?oc=5)
*Islam · Nation.Cymru*

The Senedd has rejected calls for a Wales-specific inquiry into grooming gangs. That means victims and families in Wales may still be left without a focused public investigation into what police, councils and social services knew and failed to stop.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** 'Sarah' was subjected to exactly the kind of horror such inquiries must confront: grooming, repeated rape, forced sharia marriages, forced conversion to Islam, forced abortions and then failures by authorities.

**Who this hits:** This affects survivors of grooming gangs in Wales, families still asking why warnings were missed, and girls currently at risk if institutions remain frightened of naming patterns of abuse. It also affects ordinary parents who want to know whether local authorities will protect children without political embarrassment.

**Angle:** Our line is that refusing an inquiry protects institutions, not victims. Viewers will understand why labels such as 'Islamophobia' can silence legitimate questions about grooming, sharia, forced conversion and police failure — and why Christians should insist that truth-telling is part of justice.

**Opening line:** "Why did Welsh politicians say no to a grooming gangs inquiry?"

**Title:** *Wales rejects grooming gangs inquiry: what are they afraid to uncover?*

### 2. [Disabled MPs voted against assisted dying bill by two to one, records show](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxPZUFUM0k2OEdXLXNjcW4zU1ZSZWctQkUxMjE2SWxpS2J3N1lYVHFJMUswQlBYd3hIN250Vkx6NkNXcDhfX1A5ZTUzTkFkS211STdTY1ozckZTU0dqTDY0aGdWMmtiQXFzMzJxVkdJM2ZndkFNQWlvbXZxZUdoVTZCTENNZnhQczdCS2Z4M0RGNHNiY0I3a1NmaG9hY2dYMXN4WFBMemdLYV9DeTdRMFhtb3NR?oc=5)
*End of life · Disability News Service*

Records show that disabled MPs voted against the assisted dying bill by a two-to-one margin. That is significant because disabled people are often the very people campaigners claim assisted suicide laws would protect.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Indi Gregory, Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Rashid Abbasi were not assisted-suicide cases, but they show what happens when seriously ill and disabled lives are judged through a system that can overrule families and patients.

**Who this hits:** This affects disabled people, elderly relatives, and families caring for someone who fears becoming a burden. It also matters for churchgoers whose MPs may soon face further pressure to back assisted suicide in another form.

**Angle:** Our line is that Parliament should listen carefully when disabled MPs are warning against this law. Viewers will see that opposition to assisted suicide is not just a 'religious' concern; it is a safeguarding concern about pressure, fear, poor care and the need for proper palliative support.

**Opening line:** "Disabled MPs just exposed the assisted suicide debate’s hidden fault line."

**Title:** *Disabled MPs voted against assisted suicide — we should listen*

### 3. [Musk's X 'disgusting' for shunning meeting, says minister - as she vows more laws governing internet](https://news.sky.com/story/musks-x-disgusting-for-shunning-meeting-says-minister-as-she-vows-more-laws-governing-internet-13588995)
*Freedom of speech · Sky News (UK)*

A government minister criticised X for not attending a meeting about online attacks on the UK's lifeboat charity and said more internet laws would be introduced. The practical question is whether future regulation targets genuinely criminal abuse or expands pressure against lawful unpopular speech.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Anthony Stevens was arrested in front of his family over tweets defending free speech, while Kristie Higgs lost her school job over a private Facebook post about relationships and sex education.

**Who this hits:** This affects Christians who post biblical views online, parents sharing concerns about schools, and workers whose employers monitor social media. It may not change anything tomorrow, but it signals more political appetite to regulate what happens online.

**Angle:** Our line is that abuse and threats should be dealt with, but lawful speech must not be dragged into a state-backed censorship regime. Viewers will understand the difference between policing crime and policing opinion — and why they should ask MPs to protect lawful speech in any new internet legislation.

**Opening line:** "Could new internet laws make lawful Christian posts harder to say?"

**Title:** *More internet laws? Why Christians should be concerned*

### 4. [Event hosted in parliament hears speaker who argued 'influence of Islam' should be 'resisted'](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiyAFBVV95cUxQbl9uY3FuWGJ5NTZBd2hCbjhYU1lkTndwNFdnOG9XNk1jM3hSQTRiZ3NoejBMaFRENm9rZUNPUExibjkwdGticF93WEFwR3dYTXBvX25RaWFxV1duS24zT2U4RDBaaXRzNkU5OXhmeHEtSUUzdVNPZmcwRGhsSTVqUTJabWNEdDFlb1oteHYtZ05BZEdQS0htcy16Q2dTYTdmWE9nMW9rUmRYbDZpTzJTTF9Oa3FGVC1XRlNVTTFma29ZZTBUa0F4UA?oc=5)
*Christian Concern in the news · Middle East Eye*

Middle East Eye reports that a parliamentary event heard from a speaker who had argued that the influence of Islam should be resisted. The article presents that as controversial, raising the wider question of whether criticism of Islam is being treated as unacceptable in public life.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Luke Salmons was forced out of the police after questioning Islam in mandatory diversity training; Shaun O'Sullivan and John Steele were arrested after public comments or questions about Islam.

**Who this hits:** This affects Christians, teachers, councillors and public-sector workers who want to speak honestly about Islam, sharia, grooming gangs or religious freedom. If Parliament cannot host difficult discussion, ordinary people will get the message that they must stay silent.

**Angle:** Our line is that criticising ideas, doctrines or religious influence is not hatred against people. Viewers will understand why vague 'anti-Muslim hostility' standards are dangerous, and why Parliament must remain a place where uncomfortable truths can be examined without blasphemy codes by the back door.

**Opening line:** "When criticism of Islam reaches Parliament, why is that treated as scandal?"

**Title:** *Criticising Islam in Parliament is not a hate crime*

### 5. [Lawsuit over Belfast City Hall abortion lights: Move could see council dragged through courts to judicial review](https://news.google.?oc=5)
*Beginning of life · Belfast News Letter*

A legal challenge over Belfast City Hall being lit in connection with abortion could take the council to judicial review. The case raises whether a public civic building should be used to promote one side of a deeply contested moral issue.

**Who this hits:** This affects pro-life residents in Belfast whose rates fund the council, and Christians across the UK watching local authorities use public buildings to make ideological statements. It also gives pro-life citizens a practical example of challenging councils through lawful routes.

**Angle:** Our line is that public authorities should not celebrate abortion as though unborn life does not matter. Viewers will understand that council decisions are not neutral just because they are wrapped in lights and symbols — and they can ask their own councillors what policy governs political or moral displays on public buildings.

**Opening line:** "Should a city hall be lit up to celebrate abortion?"

**Title:** *Belfast abortion lights lawsuit: can councils promote abortion?*

# 🎯 Top 5 to comment on

### 1. [I’m a grooming gang survivor. This is why Rory Stewart is wrong](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilAFBVV95cUxOamdwTlpmRHN3d19VZEpXYUthWjYyTEFPN0R5OEM1OENkWVNwZU94OWZ6WkluY0xkeWpMc2dGa3dHOGVjUmlKUzRXbFpsNUdoZ3pza3FaY2NlSGlKVG05eXpwb1UxdUJOUlJRVEFYNy1wQ2JXYUNyalRMWUVBNVRTR2UxYmhoY1VkN3J6TFduVWp5VGZX?oc=5)
*Islam · UnHerd*

A grooming gang survivor has challenged Rory Stewart’s comments and warned that public figures still fail to face the religious and cultural realities behind some grooming gang abuse. The piece argues that victims are silenced when concerns about Islam, sharia or forced conversion are dismissed as prejudice.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** 'Sarah' was subjected to exactly this: she was groomed, repeatedly raped, forced into sharia marriages, forcibly converted to Islam and made to undergo eight abortions.

**Who this hits:** This affects survivors who are still trying to be believed, and parents whose daughters may be vulnerable to exploitation while authorities fear saying the wrong thing. It also affects social workers, police and councillors who need the courage to name what is happening without hiding behind labels.

**Angle:** We should say plainly that protecting girls matters more than protecting reputations or ideologies. Viewers will understand why vague language about “community tensions” can leave victims abandoned, and why inquiries must be able to examine grooming, sharia, forced conversion and institutional failure without being shut down by accusations of Islamophobia.

**Opening line:** "What happens when a grooming victim is told the truth is too dangerous to say?"

**Title:** *Grooming gangs: why victims must not be silenced*

### 2. [Where you live affects what you children are taught](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikwFBVV95cUxPWlc3NUFSYUlaRjhMNjkzMVVZdnVJbjJnVEVuODFoUnJLaWtsZkJ6Y1pqbjRXc0dGajhuMWlROHBxZ0lwaUd1bDhwUC0zd3p3WjRTNV9TLWlmOFZwUXpjemNjQzJMZDFpcXhGLUZocXZyVkliVzJuSmljWHBJUW1oMGNIaHBoY21PSU92ejlDZjhSUms?oc=5)
*Christian Concern in the news · Christian Concern*

Christian Concern has highlighted how children’s classroom teaching on relationships, sex and identity can vary dramatically depending on the school and local authority. The story points to the postcode lottery parents face when trying to know what their children are being taught.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Izzy Montague challenged her son’s primary school after LGBT issues were promoted to children as young as five with no right to opt out; Kristie Higgs lost her job after sharing concerns about RSE on Facebook.

**Who this hits:** This affects parents choosing schools, grandparents worried about what children are hearing, and Christian teachers under pressure to promote lessons they believe are harmful. It is especially practical for families with children starting or moving school this year.

**Angle:** Our line is that parents, not the state, have the primary responsibility for children’s moral formation. Viewers gain a concrete next step: ask schools what materials are being used, whether outside providers are involved, and how parents can see lesson content before it is taught.

**Opening line:** "Two schools, two postcodes, two very different messages to your child."

**Title:** *What is your child’s school teaching about sex and identity?*

### 3. ['I was given electric shocks to knock the homosexuality out of my brain'](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiXEFVX3lxTE5YcmNaLTRaVzRhY0tIZU8wcWNWcFluMEZqaEtJNFY5dVJMNXR5WnhIbmFXUVR0SUFRTFJlLU9fQ3p1OGdRZVMzdEV0b1ZJY05GbHpMOHBKbmtJUm1v?oc=5)
*Sexuality · BBC*

The BBC reported the testimony of someone who says he was subjected to electric shocks in an attempt to change his sexuality. Such stories are often used to argue for broad conversion therapy or conversion practices bans.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Matthew Grech is being prosecuted in Malta for sharing his Christian testimony of leaving a homosexual lifestyle, showing how conversion therapy laws can move from stopping abuse to criminalising speech, prayer and testimony.

**Who this hits:** This affects pastors, parents, counsellors and Christians who want to pray or talk honestly with someone who asks for help. It also affects people with unwanted sexual feelings or gender confusion who may lose the freedom to seek Christian pastoral support.

**Angle:** We should condemn coercive and abusive practices without allowing horrific historic abuse to become an excuse for banning consensual Christian conversation. Viewers will understand the vital distinction politicians often blur: electric shocks are abuse, but prayer, testimony and pastoral care are not.

**Opening line:** "Can we condemn abuse without criminalising prayer?"

**Title:** *Conversion therapy bans: where does abuse end and criminalising prayer begin?*

### 4. [Why MPs finally said no to assisted dying](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxQa0RWMEg0LXJ4WjE5aENOaHJEOFlRQkswLWpJa25GRU9yZ252QUJoVjhkZHZkZEZtdXAtd0gwYVNfbmdKeWYwZkhqX3hlZ0dGMGF4OXlhQTg1akdHQzBHLTk2ZW5JajNGQWpUdkZ1dV9lVFBTMkZscGtraXJyODJJN2FUaEc3RFRJNm45ME5mVEstYjlUb0pia0V0WUZ1Rm9Q?oc=5)
*End of life · Premier Christianity Magazine*

Premier Christianity reported on why MPs rejected assisted dying, exploring the arguments that persuaded Parliament to say no. The debate centred on safeguards, pressure on vulnerable people and whether the law should allow doctors to help end life.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Indi Gregory, Sudiksha Thirumalesh and Rashid Abbasi’s families all faced hospitals and courts making life-and-death decisions against the wishes of patients or parents, showing how vulnerable people can be overruled in medical settings.

**Who this hits:** This affects elderly relatives, disabled people, seriously ill patients and families sitting beside a hospital bed trying to make decisions under pressure. It also affects voters who need to know what their MP believes before the issue returns.

**Angle:** Our line is that Parliament was right to reject a law that would make some people feel they are a burden. Viewers will see why “choice” can become pressure in practice, and why better palliative care—not assisted suicide—is the compassionate answer.

**Opening line:** "Would your grandmother be offered care, or a quicker way to die?"

**Title:** *Why MPs were right to reject assisted dying*

### 5. [Labour peer demands Patriot Platform is outlawed as terror group after Dover and Portsmouth protests](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxPUWJIRlZpeUxFeFY1UjMyMUtIVE5qbHFzcExyY1l2RmUxMEJ6V3U5WS1zWnp0VFUwaWFDZm0tTW1YVElmTXVLLXdoTWk4a0RLcWRYMlI5NFZDdEctS2NnQXdRZWt2SGkwb1huTS15ak9lZlpaOEdWMXZ1ZHFHNDRDTHZmM184aUxnYzBPc3hIMWJGTVdxWkFJLTIzaw?oc=5)
*Freedom of speech · GB News*

A Labour peer has called for Patriot Platform to be outlawed as a terrorist group following protests in Dover and Portsmouth. The story raises questions about when protest, even protest many people dislike, is treated as extremism or terrorism.

**⚖️ OUR CASE:** Bernard Randall was reported to Prevent, the government’s terrorism watchdog, after a school sermon telling pupils they did not have to accept LGBT ideology; Aaron Edwards was threatened with a counter-terrorism referral over a tweet on human sexuality.

**Who this hits:** This affects Christians who speak publicly, attend protests, preach, post online or work in institutions using extremism policies. It also affects parents and teachers who fear that ordinary moral or political disagreement could be treated as a safeguarding or terrorism concern.

**Angle:** We do not have to endorse a group to defend the principle that terrorism powers must not become a shortcut for suppressing unpopular views. Viewers will understand how expansive extremism language can travel from controversial protests to sermons, tweets and classroom speech.

**Opening line:** "When does unpopular protest become “terrorism” in the eyes of the state?"

**Title:** *Are terrorism labels being used to shut down dissent?*
